NBA superstar LeBron James and ESPN are reportedly finalizing a deal for a comprehensive documentary that will chronicle his anticipated final chapter with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Sources indicate that talks are at the "1-yard line”, with the project expected to emulate the acclaimed "The Last Dance" series, which offered an intimate look into Michael Jordan's career with the Chicago Bulls.

James, 41, recently inked a two-year, $8 million contract with the Sixers, a move widely expected to be the concluding phase of his legendary career.

A dedicated camera crew is slated to follow the four-time NBA MVP as he embarks on a quest for an unprecedented fifth championship ring, according to reports.

open image in gallery The 'Last Dance' documentary that followed Michael Jordan's career was widely acclaimed ( AFP/Getty )

The documentary is set to extend beyond his tenure in Philadelphia, incorporating extensive footage from across the 22-time All-Star's illustrious career. This will include never-before-seen clips of the league's all-time leading scorer, promising a deep dive into his journey.

With a career that has kept him in the public eye since his debut as a 17-year-old Sports Illustrated cover athlete in 2002, James has generated an abundance of material.

He previously secured NBA titles with all three of his former teams: the Los Angeles Lakers (2018-26), Miami Heat (2010-14), and Cleveland Cavaliers (2003-10, 2014-18), most recently in 2019-20 with the Lakers.

James announced his move to Philadelphia last Friday, with the NBA franchise officially confirming the deal on Monday.

Speaking about his desire to push for further glory, James said: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time.

His dedication was evident even before the official announcement, with James posting workout videos on his Instagram story Monday morning, captioned: "It's that time again. 4:12 AM. Let's get it."

Team owner Josh Harris echoed James’s positivity, saying, "I cannot wait to see LeBron alongside Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and our talented roster as we work to deliver a championship for Philly."

Last season, the Sixers finished 45-37, ultimately being swept in the second round by the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks.

News.title: Ohio man argues it was poverty not a crime that led to a ‘house of horrors’ 16 kids were rescued from squalor
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

An attorney representing one of the Ohio"house of horrors" defendants says it's poverty, not criminality, that led to the disturbing discovery at his property last month and the rescue of 16 children from squalor.

One month ago, police arrested Gary Siders, 73, along with his wife, Christina Siders, 67; son, Gary Siders II, 36; and daughter-in-law, Elizabeth Siders, 33, after 16 children were found living at their home in Hamden, Ohio, in deplorable conditions.

The elder Siders is facing 16 counts of child endangerment. His attorney, Dorian Baum, told WCMH that Siders' is being prosecuted because he's poor, not because he is negligent.

“Everyone should take a deep breath and step back because unfortunately, when all this comes out, [what] we’re going to see is a state entity which is criminalizing poverty and little more,” Baum said.

Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson said the children looked "almost feral" when they were rescued by authorities. Police described parts of the house that were inaccessible due to the trash accumulation inside.

open image in gallery From top left: Gary Siders II, Elizabeth Siders, Christina Siders, and Gary Siders. The four family members have been charged with numerous counts of child endangerment after 16 children were found living in deplorable conditions with them in a house in Vinton County, Ohio, in late June ( Vinton County Sheriff )

“They looked like almost feral animals,” Wilson said of the children. “It was terrible.”

He said during a press conference that the children were largely contained to a single 12 x 12 room

Baum has accused Wilson of sensationalizing the case despite the fact that the Siders have not even been indicted yet.

“This is not a matter that the AG should have stuck his nose in because everything from these videos to other evidence that I’ve been privy to, minimally pre-indictment, is that the AG didn’t know what the hell he was talking about, period. End of story,” he told the outlet.

The lawyer also blasted local police for not securing the crime scene since the discovery. Wilson told the outlet that the county didn’t have the manpower to staff an officer at the home.

“Those officers are out handling regular calls. They can’t be sitting on that house the whole time,” Wilson told the outlet. “If somebody goes in there, there’s a really good chance that they’re going to get hurt.”

The children — whose parents are Elizabeth Siders and Gary Siders II — have been taken into protective custody. Seven of the children needed hospitalization, with one who was in critical condition.

open image in gallery A lawyer for one of the suspects said it was poverty, not criminal actions, that led to the conditions at the home ( AP )

open image in gallery Police described parts of the house that were inaccessible due to the trash accumulation inside ( AP )

Vinton County Local School District confirmed to local media that it has no records showing that any of the 16 children — the oldest is 18 — ever attended school at the district.

Ohio officials have approved $1 million for the care of the children while their permanent custody is being determined.

Police did not reveal how they first became aware of the Siders' home.

All four suspects have pleaded not guilty. An attorney for Gary II on Friday filed a motion notifying the court that his client is pursuing a mental health competency screening to ensure he is fit to stand trial.

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

Sports.title: Premier League stars face at least 10-MATCH bans for ‘aggravated breaches’ as FA impose new punishment
Sports.content:
CRACKDOWN Premier League stars face at least 10-MATCH bans for ‘aggravated breaches’ as FA impose new punishment

Credit: Not known, clear with picture desk

FOOTBALLERS will now be hit with a whopping 10-MATCH ban as standard if they commit an aggravated breach of FA rules.

The new sanction guidelines have been introduced ahead of the 2026/27 season as part of a firmer stance against discriminatory conduct.

An aggravated breach is defined in FA Rule E3.2 as “any misconduct that includes an express or implied reference to any one or more of the following characteristics: ethnic origin, colour, race, nationality, religion or belief, sex, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, or disability“.

Recent sanction guidelines have recommended bans of between six and 12 matches to the independent regulatory commissions who dish out the punishments.





But now a standard suspension will be at least 10 matches, the FA has confirmed.

They wrote on their website: “We are committed to delivering a game free from discrimination.

“While significant progress has been made in recent years, discriminatory conduct continues to be a challenge across the game.

“Enhanced measures are necessary to tackle this abhorrent conduct, and our updated sanction guidelines will now require Regulatory Commissions to impose a standard suspension of at least 10 matches in these circumstances.”

Aggravating factors would allow commissions to impose a ban higher than 10 matches, with mitigating factors permitting them to lower it to a minimum of six matches.

Players could be slapped with bans in excess of 12 matches – or a time-based suspension – if they are charged despite already having an aggravated breach on their record.

Fulham‘s Chris Donnell was banned for six matches last year for using abusive and/or insulting words with a reference to disability.

That punishment could be heightened under the new guidelines, unless mitigating factors were presented to the commission.



Tranmere’s Sam Finlay was slapped with a 13-game ban last year for using a homophobic slur.

And Preston’s Milutin Osmajic was banned for nine matches in November after racially abusing Hannibal Mejbri.

Sports.title: Tottenham legend, 34, appointed kit man at club in Mexico after being forced to retire from football
Sports.content:
RAYADOS de Monterrey’s kit man happens to be none other than Puskas-winning Erik Lamela.

The former Tottenham star, 34, was forced into an early retirement with a hip injury that called for TWO surgeries.



But 12 months after hanging up his boots at AEK Athens, he’s back out earning his coaching badges in the guise of Monterrey’s kit man.

While he effectively operates as an assistant coach – mirroring his time at Sevilla – he can’t hold the official title yet because he lacks the required license under Article 17.1 of Liga MX statutes.



Goalkeeping coach Fabian Donelli faces the same restriction.

But with the UEFA Pro coaching course taking a year to complete, it’s possible that they’ll be named in Matias Almeyda’s coaching staff soon.

Lamela began his path to stardom at South American giants River Plate and then Roma, before joining Spurs in a deal worth £25.7million in 2013.

He arrived at White Hart Lane in the same window that Spurs sold Gareth Bale to Real Madrid for a world-record fee.

And while fellow wide man Lamela was not as productive as Bale, he still endeared himself to Tottenham fans with his tireless running and catalogue of memorable moments.

One of the fan favourites came with a 20-yard rabona in the Europa League in 2014 before he won the Puskas Award for scoring another rabona in the North London Derby seven years later.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

After over 250 Tottenham games and late-career spells at Sevilla and AEK Athens, Lamela returned to Sevilla as a coach after hanging up his boots.

His starpower caught the attention of Alejandro Sabella and then of Gerardo Tata Martino who called him up to the national team.

He made appearances in the qualifiers for the 2014 World Cup in Brazil and in the 2015 and 2016 Copa Americas, where he won the double championship.

Sports.title: England to BOYCOTT World Cup as Uefa countries unanimously in support of protest against Fifa’s sale plan
Sports.content:
UEFA nations will BOYCOTT the World Cup if Gianni Infantino proceeds with his controversial plans.

Earlier this week it emerged that the under-fire Fifa president wants to create a sister company to take charge of its tournaments, including the World Cup, before selling off a significant chunk of the new subsidiary.



Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin immediately slammed the project, releasing a statement claiming that Fifa had “crossed the line”.

European football’s governing body hosted a virtual meeting with its 55 member associations today.



And according to The Times, a decision was made to boycott Fifa competitions, including the World Cup, should Infantino proceed with his plan.

Fifa claim that they only need a majority of their 211 member associations to vote in favour of the plans for them to go through – meaning they can still launch the lucrative Fifa Forward Enterprise without Uefa’s backing.

But European nations would plunge the World Cup into crisis with a boycott, which would theoretically see the next edition of world football’s biggest event take place without the likes of England, France and Spain.

This is likely to see Infantino’s privatisation plan collapse.

Infantino, 56, reportedly wants to receive $4.2billion (£3.1bn) of funding for the project as soon as October.

Fifa are said to have brought US bank JPMorgan onboard in an advisory capacity.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Uefa statement in full UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale. It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football. National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. But our opposition goes far beyond process. The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders. This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation. As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership. Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination. There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments. Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.

Should plans be given the green light, Thrive Eternal, whose CEO Joshua Kushner is Donald Trump‘s son-in-law Jared Kushner‘s brother, are tipped to purchase a 20 per cent stake.

Infantino has developed a close relationship with Trump amid this summer’s World Cup, with the pair even watching the final together from a suite.

Last year Infantino awarded the US president inaugural Fifa Peace Prize.

Fifa claim their 211 Member Associations stand to gain $40m (£30m) each if they signed up to the Forward Enterprise proposal within 53 days.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham slammed Fifa’s plan in a social media post.



Burnham wrote on X: “Let me say this very directly.

“Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.

“Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”

In addition to Uefa’s hardline stance the AFC, Asian football’s governing body, has also expressed concern at Fifa’s plan.



An extract of a letter to his 47 member member associations by AFC chief Sheikh Salman read: “Furthermore, the AFC is deeply concerned that Fifa’s unilateral actions appear to undermine the very foundations of continental football, which are based on solidarity, co-operation and transparency.

“Moreover, such an initiative will not succeed without the support of all the confederations, which is not the case now.”

Infantino responded to criticism on Wednesday with a baffling monologue.

He said: “Fifa Forward Enterprise or FFE is actually a proposal, an offer.

“It’s part of a democratic process, a consultation process and above all it is an opportunity but not an obligation.



“If and only if it is approved by the majority of our 211 Member Associations (MAs) and the Fifa Council, it would be a Fifa-owned and controlled subsidiary consolidating Fifa’s commercial and event operations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In the next (Fifa) Forward cycle alone distributions would rise $8m per MA to $20m.

“Additionally, each MA will also have the option to access a further $20m through the Fifa Fast Forward Programme, taking the potential funding to $40m per MA for this next cycle.”

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Gunners star asks for transfer to former European champions as Gyokeres gets new role
Sports.content:
ARSENAL flop Fabio Vieira has his heart set on a move to Hamburg this summer.

The midfielder, 26, spent last season on loan with the German club and wants to join them permanently.



Vieira scored seven goals in 31 appearances for Hamburg last term and they are pushing to bring him back.

Talks are underway with Arsenal, but so far there has been no agreement over a fee.



Last summer’s loan deal included the option for the move to be made permanent this summer for €20million (£17m).

Hamburg want to pay less than that and Vieira is into the final 12 months of his contract with Arsenal.



The Gunners splashed out £34m to sign the Portuguese playmaker from Porto in 2022 – but he has struggled to perform.

During his tenure in North London, he managed just three goals in 49 appearances.

Hamburg was Vieira’s second loan spell in as many years after he went back to Porto for the 2024-25 season.

The midfielder is currently training with Arsenal at their pre-season camp in Spain and they will face Girona this weekend.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

TZO GOOD

ARSENAL new boy Christos Tzolis has been smashing his team-mates in pre-season testing.

The winger, 24, joined the Gunners last week from Club Brugge as part of a deal that is worth £34m.

The Greek star has gone straight into training and was with the squad at London Colney last week before they flew to Spain at the weekend.

Mikel Arteta’s players have been put through their paces by the club’s new fitness coaches – and Tzolis has been the man to beat.



Gunners defender Ben White said: “Christos has been amazing.

“He came in, did all the testing, and beat everyone. So he is fitting in really well and everyone is really happy for him to be here.”

Tzolis featured for Arsenal in a secret behind-closed-doors friendly last week against MK Dons.

The Gunners ran out 3-0 winners against the League One club and Tzolis grabbed an assist.



FEEL THE BERN

TEEN star Mylo Bernard is closing in on a move to Arsenal.

The striker, 16, had been on the books of Crystal Palace but is now making the move across London.

Bernard is a talented prospect and he made his debut for England’s Under-16s earlier this year.

The Gunners have been pushing hard to make signings at academy level to boost the performances of their young teams.



Cardiff City teenager Axel Donczew, 16, is also joining and the attacking midfielder has already played senior football.

Bernard will come in and play for Arsenal’s Under-18 side – but will be encouraged to push for the Under-21s, too.

PITCH PERFECT

VIKTOR GYOKERES has a new role at Arsenal after taking up the task of being dressing room DJ.

William Saliba is usually in charge of the music before matches – but the defender is set for a spell on the sidelines.

The France star aggravated a back injury at the World Cup and is likely to miss the first few months of the season.



It leaves the Arsenal squad needing an interim resident DJ.

And, during a Q&A on Reddit, the new man was revealed.

In a video reply to a fan question, defender White said: “When Willy isn’t here, the DJ is one of the kitmen or Viktor, maybe.”

HOWE ABOUT THAT

MIKEL ARTETA will have to face a host of unknown quantities during Arsenal’s title defence this season.



Following Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit, only nine of the current Premier League bosses were in place at their club at the start of last season.

Of those nine, just six of them are from the 17 teams that remained in the division last term.

Most of Arsenal’s direct rivals have changed bosses in the last few months, including Chelsea, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester City.

It leaves Arteta with plenty of homework to do on his opposite numbers ahead of the season kicking off next month.

Arteta is known for his incredible attention to detail and pre-match preparation, but even this will be a huge undertaking for the Spaniard.



The 44-year-old is now English football’s longest-serving manager and urged his team to reach a “different dimension” this term.

But making sure his squad is prepared for the unfamiliar opponents will be a massive part of securing even more success.

GRANIT XHAKA is still influencing the future of Arsenal, three years on from his Emirates exit.



Academy ace Callan Hamill claimed Xhaka is his role model upon signing his first professional contract with the Gunners.

Sports.title: Argentina stars could be banned for NEXT World Cup after Falklands banner and ‘assault’ on Spain players in final
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA stars face being BANNED from the next World Cup despite being co-hosts over their Falklands banner and behaviour in the final.

Lionel Messi and Co are being probed by Fifa over their antics towards the end of the tournament.



The team endured a sour end to the tournament as they were beaten 1-0 by Spain at the MetLife Stadium.

But Argentina came under fire in the semi-finals after their 2-1 win over England when a handful of players held up a contoversial sign.



It read: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates as “The Falklands are Argentine”.

Lionel Scaloni’s men – who had already enraged a number of teams over some favourable decisions throughout the tournament – attracted more negative headlines in the final.



Argentina were involved in ugly scenes after the final whistle as they were seen brawling with Spain players.

Leandro Paredes was filmed grabbing the throat of Spain defender Eric Garcia while footage showed Nahuel Molina struck Rodri as he ran past during the celebrations.

Fifa have the power to issue a global ban for Argentina players who were involved in the banner and violence after opening proceedings.

But the team won’t play in another Fifa match until the 2030 World Cup because they are co-hosting the tournament alongside Spain, Portugal, Morocco and Uruguay.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That means Argentina won’t play any qualifying matches in the build up.

So the next available match for players to be banned could be Argentina’s opening match of the 2030 World Cup.

Argentina were fined £20,000 in 2014 after players held a banner with the same text as this tournament’s on before a friendly against Slovenia.

Cristian Romero, Lisandro Martinez and Giovani Lo Celso were all seen holding the Falklands banner.



Fifa’s statement also accused Argentina of assault against Spain players, name dropping Molina, Paredes, Thiago Almada and coach Robert Ayala.

It said: “The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has opened proceedings against the Argentinian Football Association for potential breaches of article 13 paragraph 2 c) (Using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature), article 14 paragraph 5 (Team misconduct), article 15 (Discrimination and racist abuse) and article 17 (Order and security at matches) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches of the representative team of Argentina at the FIFA World Cup 2026.“

The world champions were not totally innocent either though, with Barcelona midfielder Gavi also being charged with a charge of unsporting behaviour.

The statement continued: “The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has received the report of the appointed Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor concerning incidents that occurred during the FIFA World Cup 2026 final (Spain v. Argentina) and, following the recommendation contained therein, has opened disciplinary proceedings – for potential breaches of article 14 paragraph 1 i) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (assault) – against Argentinian players Nahuel Molina (two counts, one completed and one attempted) and Leandro Paredes (three counts) and Argentinian official Roberto Ayala (one count).

“Disciplinary proceedings have also been opened – for potential breaches of article 14 paragraph 1 b) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (unsporting behaviour) – against Argentinian players Nahuel Molina (one count) and Thiago Almada (one count) and Spanish player Pablo Martín Páez Gavira (one count).”

Sports.title: Arne Slot could make stunning return to management after Howe’s Newcastle exit with ex-Premier League boss also in mix
Sports.content:
FORMER Liverpool boss Arne Slot could be set for a return to management following Eddie Howe’s shock Newcastle exit.

The Dutch tactician was let go by the Reds in May, with Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola taking over at Anfield.



But he could be set to return to the dugout just months later after a job suddenly opened up on Thursday.

Howe and Newcastle split ways after five years as the coach stepped down from his role midway into the Magpies’ pre-season preparations.



He is set to be replaced by German Matthias Jaissle, 38, who will swap Saudi outfit Al Ahli for St James’ Park.

The relatively young coach impressed with RB Salzburg before earning a move to the PIF-owned outfit, the same PIF which bankrolls Newcastle.

But that move leaves a vacancy with Al Ahli, the back to back Asian Champions League title holders.

talkSPORT claim that Slot, who rejected a move to Fulham earlier this summer, is one of the contenders to fill in in the middle east.

He is not the only former Prem boss under consideration for the role.

Former Wolves and Nottingham Forest boss Vitor Pereira is also in the picture, with reports suggesting that contact has been made between the parties.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Pereira is no stranger to the game in Saudi Arabia.

The Portuguese, who was dismissed from his Forest job less than a month ago, arrived to the Prem from Saudi side Al Shabab, where he had spent 10 months.

And a move to Al Ahli would actually be a reunion for him, having joined for a nearly two-year spell in 2013.

Whoever joins the outfit would have the footballing talent of Former Premier League stars Francisco Trincao, Ivan Toney and Edouard Mendy at their disposal.

Sports.title: Arsenal closing in on Bruno Guimaraes transfer with Newcastle expected to accept fee of £70million-plus
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes.

The Gunners have made the midfielder a top target this summer and are expected to pay north of £70million for him.



Guimaraes is keen to join the Premier League champions and personal terms will not be an issue.

The Brazilian’s departure would be the latest blow in a nightmare summer for Newcastle.



The Magpies have already lost key men Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.

Manager Eddie Howe has joined them in heading out the exit door after news of his bombshell departure came out on Thursday morning.

Arsenal want to sign Guimaraes so that they can provide proper competition in midfield for Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi.

Both players got through a large number of minutes last season and suffered from fatigue towards the end of the campaign.

Guimaraes is viewed as a player of proven quality that could slot straight into the Arsenal team and the club are long-term admirers of him.

The Gunners have followed the Brazilian for six years and now look set to finally bring him to the Emirates.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Mikel Arteta has stressed the need for new signings as the Gunners look to retain their Premier League crown.

Speaking earlier this week, Arteta said: “From ownership, to the board, the sporting director and myself, we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals.

“We have identified where we have opportunities to grow, improve and evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. We are on it.”

Sports.title: EFL club CANCEL friendly at 24,000-capacity stadium and spark fears over opening fixture of season
Sports.content:
A FORMER Premier League club has deemed their own pitch unfit to host an upcoming pre-season friendly.

Organisers have relocated the game to a behind-closed-doors venue due to concerns over the playing surface.



Reading were due to welcome their fans back to the 24,000-capacity Select Car Leasing Stadium on Saturday for a run-out against Charlton.

But complications with the new pitch ground staff have laid during the off-season have forced the two clubs to take drastic action.



The game will now be played at an empty The Valley – Charlton’s home ground – with both clubs streaming the match for free.

Reading CEO Joe Jacobson told the club’s official website: “This is not a decision anyone at the Club wanted to make, but it is the right one.

“We’ve invested significantly in providing the team with the best possible playing surface for the season ahead.

“Unfortunately, the recent spell of hot and dry weather has slowed the development of the new pitch and, after taking expert advice, we’ve concluded that protecting it now gives us the best chance of having it in the condition we all want for the start of the League One campaign.

“We’re grateful to Charlton Athletic for their understanding, cooperation and support in helping us rearrange the fixture.

“We also thank our supporters for their patience and continued backing, and we look forward to welcoming everyone back to the Select Car Leasing Stadium when we begin our League One campaign against Luton Town.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Reading kick off their competitive season with a Carabao Cup first-round tie at Bromley on August 8.

The pitch has just over two weeks to grow in before the Royals’ first home game of the campaign against Luton the following Saturday.

Sports.title: UEFA release statement confirming World Cup boycott in major blow for Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
UEFA release statement confirming World Cup boycott in major blow for Gianni Infantino

Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off a stake of the World Cup has been met with a furious backlash - and now England and other major nations are ready to snub future tournaments

View Image UEFA nations have confirmed they will boycott the World Cup over Gianni Infantino's plans (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

UEFA have confirmed in a statement that England and other nations will not compete in FIFA competitions, saying they "unanimously and unequivocally reject" plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



It is the latest blow for Gianni Infantino, the FIFA president who has already been heavily scrutinised for happenings at the recent World Cup.

‌



UEFA's statement means not only would England and other countries snub future variations of the World Cup but also other FIFA tournaments such as the Club World Cup, which Infantino and Co have been trying to showcase recently.

‌



Their statement in full reads: "UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions

"UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

‌



"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

"But our opposition goes far beyond process.

‌



"The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

"This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

‌



"Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

"As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

"Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

‌



"There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

"Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."

Sports.title: Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure
Sports.content:
Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure

Eddie Howe led a Newcastle team that was blossoming and on the up for several years, but he's presided over a decline over the last 12 months, which has ended with him stepping away

View 4 Images Eddie Howe's five year stay at Newcastle boss will come to an end (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Eddie Howe's time at Newcastle has come to an end - a tenure that promised so much has endured in a gradual decline over the past year.

‌



Even before the Magpies were well beaten by Bristol City on Wednesday night, it did not seem a happy camp. Howe has taken Newcastle from a side fighting relegation to one making the Champions League knockouts, but his hands have appeared increasingly tied.

‌



In recent years the club have appeared hamstrung and this summer Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have been sold, while Bruno Guimaraes may yet follow.

‌



Newcastle's Saudi Arabian owners have spoken about being the world's best team sooner rather than later, but the club are tracking in the opposite direction right now. Howe has enjoyed the affection of the Toon Army, taking them to heights they haven't seen since Sir Bobby Robson managed them in the early 2000s.

Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players READ MORE :

Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure READ MORE :

But last year's 12th-place finish followed years that have seen Newcastle lack consistency. Howe's full-season finishes read fourth, seventh, fifth and then comes their drop down to the bottom half. That has appeared a lot to stomach, the repercussions have been obvious, and Howe has called time.

The highs have been monumental, but the lows over the past year especially have not aligned with a club who want to be up there with the elite. We delve into the five moments that saw Howe scale the mountain, before falling down it at an alarming rate.

‌



His first January window

Newcastle walked in 2022 as a side in the relegation zone, but no team in the bottom three of the Premier League has ever had such an injection of cash given their takeover only months earlier. They spent it excellently though, recruitment the club conducted wasn't just to save them, but to set them up for the years that followed.

View 4 Images Newcastle signed Bruno Guimaraes from Lyon in 2022 (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Image)

Kieran Trippier was the first statement buy of the Saudi-era and the versatile full-back was signed for only £12million, which was excellent value. That same window they landed Guimaraes from Lyon, who was well thought of, but didn't have Europe's elite crying out for him. He's become the cornerstone of everything good that happened under Howe.

‌



Securing Champions League football

A year after securing a mid-table spot, armed by the addition of Alexander Isak, Newcastle begun 2022/23 in impressive fashion, losing just once in their first 24 games to start the season. They mixed it with the likes of Manchester City, Arsenal and Manchester United. They would later claim wins over the Red Devils and hammer Tottenham 6-1 in a memorable afternoon at St James' Park.

Qualifying for the Champions League was certainly on the radar, but there's no doubt Howe accelerated that timeline. Whether that changed the perception of what the club should be achieving, only those inside the four walls know, but they seized on poor years from the likes of Liverpool and Chelsea to finish fourth.

Winning the Carabao Cup

Nothing ignites tenures and gets fans excited more than a trophy and for all the times Newcastle had finished in the top four over the past three decades, never did they have their moment in the sun. Well, Howe changes that, and it was a managerial masterclass that day at Wembley.

‌



View 4 Images Dan Burn was on the scoresheet as Newcastle's claim Carabao Cup glory (Image: Getty Images)

Having beaten Arsenal home and away, they were still underdogs when they came up against Liverpool, who had set the pace in the league and were tipped to claim the first trophy of the Arne Slot era. Instead goals from Dan Burn and Isak set Newcastle on their way to the most memorable of triumphs.

Isak's exit and failed replacements

Only months after scoring to down Liverpool in the final, one of 27 goals that year, the Swede decided he wanted out. He was prepared to down tools to get his own way and this was the first time in the Saudi-era that Newcastle had one of their biggest names wanting to quit. Previously they had been upwardly mobile and it seemed everyone was here for the journey, but it appeared not.

‌



Isak's desire to leave was a distraction. Newcastle claimed he wasn't for sale, but then let him leave on deadline day. In return they managed to land Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa - between them last year they scored 14 times and some games saw them sat on the bench alongside each other. Before that Newcastle had tried - but failed - to sign Hugo Ekitike and Benjamin Sesko. It was an unmitigated mess, and the season that followed reflected that chaos.

View 4 Images Newcastle have struggled to recover from the loss of Alexander Isak (Image: 2024 Getty Images)

Sunderland complete the double

In a Premier League campaign that saw Newcastle lose 17 times, going down to Sunderland at St James' Park was perhaps the lowest point. The Black Cats were enjoying an excellent debut year, securing European football, and followed up their win at the Stadium of Light by silencing their rivals.

Article continues below

Sunderland scored their winner in the 90th minute - which was the fourth time in just over two months that Newcastle had conceded a losing goal after the 80th minute. The loss to their arch rivals was also during a period whereby they were beaten nine times in 12 games and their season dwindled to one of irrelevance.

Sports.title: Tribute to a true footballing legend, Kevin Keegan
Sports.content:
Tribute to a true footballing legend, Kevin Keegan

To celebrate the life of a true footballing legend, we have produced a stunning special souvenir tribute.

View 2 Images Newcastle United striker Kevin Keegan, 1982. (Photo by Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

As Britain’s only multi -Ballon d’Or winner, his deeds on the pitch for Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle were legendary in their own right. But the beauty of Keegan is that he was about far more than kicking or heading a ball.

‌



He was a man of the people, the authentic working class idol who always put the fans first and was never too busy to turn down an autograph request or, in more recent times, a selfie.

‌



His career started as an unknown £33,000 signing from Scunthorpe United to Liverpool. There have been worse pieces of transfer business. Keegan was the kingpin as the Reds dominated British football through the 1970s, helping to inspire a whole new generation of worldwide fans as Liverpool started to turn into the global force they have become today. At the height of his powers, KK walked out of his Anfield comfort zone to play in Germany. A trailblazer again. At first his new team-mates shunned him, jealous of this big-money capture. They quickly realised Der Englander was too good to keep down. Twice, while with SV Hamburg, he won European Footballer of the Year.

‌



View 2 Images

Always ready for a challenge, Keegan upped sticks again to help little Southampton push for the league title with the best team, and the most enthralling football, witnessed down on the south coast. His final chapter as a player was at the other end of the country with Newcastle United, the beginning of a journey which turned him into the Pied Piper of the north-east, a man to galvanise an entire region down on its luck. He was to return as manager, giving the Toon Army what many rate as their greatest team - Ginola, Ferdinand, Beardsley, Asprilla, Shearer. ‘The Entertainers’, they became known as. Thrilling, fearless, goal-laden football which while it lasted made Newcastle everybody else’s second favourite side. You score two, we’ll get four. Wor Kev, as the Geordies called him, never did things by half. He may not have lifted the Premier League as a manager, while his 20-month reign as England boss was hardly stellar. But Keegan’s impact in the dugout can never be under-estimated. He won promotions and the league title in his first season in charge of Newcastle, Fulham and Manchester City - the only man in history to achieve such a feat. His drive, ambition and presence reinvigorated the three clubs.

‌



You will struggle to find anybody with a bad word to say about Kevin Keegan.

This special edition covers off the many highs, and the occasional low, of a career in which Special K was the most popular footballer of his generation and then a manager the fan on the street could warm to and identify with.

To slightly alter the words of the great man himself, We’d Love It if you enjoy reading about the many memories. LOVE IT!

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford posts Barcelona farewell message as dream return goes up in smoke
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford posts Barcelona farewell message as dream return goes up in smoke

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United after Barcelona opted against making his loan move permanent with the forward issuing a statement on the matter

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford had been hoping to secure a permanent move to Barcelona (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has posted a farewell message on social media to Barcelona and their fans - making it clear that a permanent move has been overlooked.

‌



The forward was out in the cold at Manchester United 12 months ago having clashed with Ruben Amorim and, after a brief loan at Aston Villa, was able to secure a blockbuster season-long move to the Catalan giants.

‌



Inserted in the loan agreement was the chance to make the move to the Nou Camp permanent, but Barcelona opted against paying the £26million it would've took. Rashford had been open about the fact he would've relished the chance to play for the La Liga side beyond this season.

‌



Rashford scored 14 times in 49 games, making some valuable contributions as he scored in an El Clasico win, with Barcelona retaining their La Liga title. However was never a guaranteed starter as the team had Lamine Yamal and Raphinha on the wings, which led to increased competition, and he's issued his thanks as he accepts a return to Manchester.

Man Utd ready to offload quartet including player they refused to swap for Carlos Baleba READ MORE :

Man Utd prepare to take advantage of Newcastle carnage with own signing who wants out READ MORE :

He wrote on his Instagram: “I’m very grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here such a positive and memorable experience. I've enjoyed every moment and will take many special memories with me. I wish the club and all its supporters the very best of luck and every success in the season ahead. Visca el Barca”

A permanent move to Barcelona became all the more challenging when they spent £70m on Anthony Gordon, who moved from Newcastle. Rashford's compatriot plays out wide and it suggested that the Catalans had other players on their radar given they could've had the United loanee for much less.

‌



Their next target is Julian Alvarez with the Spanish champions needing to replace Robert Lewandowski, who was allowed to depart. The Argentine is at rivals Atletico Madrid, who are determined not to sell with any move likely to well exceed the £100m mark.

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford fell out of favour when Ruben Amorim was in charge (Image: PA)

Returning to Old Trafford, where he has not played for well over 18 months, is made easier by the fact Amorim has been moved on. The Portuguese coach froze out Rashford and was public in his views, claiming he and the forward did not see football the same way.

‌



Michael Carrick is now in charge and whilst that presents a new era for Rashford, there has been no clear indication yet over whether he will be introduced back into the fold. The likes of Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha were crucial in United's run of form that saw them finish third last season, and are likely ahead of Rashford in the pecking order.

Since making his debut in 2016 Rashford has scored 138 times in 426 games for his boyhood club.

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to offload quartet including player they refused to swap for Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to offload quartet including player they refused to swap for Carlos Baleba

Manchester United are willing to sanction exits for four of their young stars, including Toby Collyer, who they refused to sell 12 months ago

View 2 Images Dan Gore and Toby Collyer are both free to leave Manchester

Manchester United will listen to offers for young quartet Harry Amass, Dan Gore, Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek as Michael Carrick continues to put his stamp on the squad.

The Red Devils have continued their push to sign more midfield talent this summer, adding Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos whilst at least one more could also arrive. Reinforcements in attack and at left-back are also on their radar.

All have had loan spells away and both temporary and permanent exits are on the cards, reports the Daily Mail. Goalkeeper Vitek impressed at Bristol City last season and enquiries have been made for him. Harry Amass, who was at Norwich previously, is also of interest.

Collyer has returned from a season that saw him have loan spells at West Brom and Hull, but United have previously been adamant he's not for sale.

Man Utd prepare to take advantage of Newcastle carnage with own signing who wants out READ MORE :

Man United slammed by Gary Neville over failure to land no-brainer Chelsea signing READ MORE :

He was seen as a potential bargaining chip when United eye a £100million plus move for Carlos Baleba at Brighton, but those at Old Trafford refused to use him as part of the deal. Collyer came through the ranks at the Amex having been born in Worthing, just 10 miles down the road.

He left in 2022 and those in Manchester were surprised when the chance to sign him came up with the 22-year-old considered one of the best midfielders in his age group.

United's signings in the middle of the pitch do still leave him with plenty ahead of him in the pecking order and, from a career development point of view, it looks as if he's best served playing away from Old Trafford.

View 2 Images Radek Vitek impressed at Bristol City last year

Baleba is among the names that United have again been linked with, albeit the Cameroon star did not enjoy his best campaign. His level did drop in the month after he was linked with a move to Manchester, which Brighton ultimately never entertained.

The young quartet of Collyer, Amass, Gore and Vitek will ultimately remain training with United until the first-team stars who were in World Cup action rejoin the squad as they enjoy extended breaks.

Sports.title: England told they must BOYCOTT 2030 World Cup in response to Gianni Infantino plan
Sports.content:
England told they must BOYCOTT 2030 World Cup in response to Gianni Infantino plan

England have been told to consider boycotting the next World Cup by several former FA bosses as organisations unite to reject FIFA's proposal, which is led by Gianni Infantino

View 2 Images A boycott of the World Cup by leading nations would put a spanner in FIFA's plans (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Several former FA chiefs have urged England to snub the next World Cup in response to Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in FIFA's major tournaments.

‌



The FIFA president has announced his proposal, which has been widely condemned across the footballing world, as he seeks to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events - and outside investors will be able to purchase those stakes.

‌



UEFA have called out FIFA and that has led to backlash from federations in Asia and North America. The FA have said they were "completely unaware of this proposal" and they are "deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance".

‌



Several men who have stood at the top of English football have taken aim at FIFA's plans and have backed extreme measures in a bid to rebel against FIFA - which includes not playing at the next World Cup that is being held in Spain and Portugal.

19 countries have pulled out of World Cup as UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino boycott READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott READ MORE :

David Bernstein, who took a public stand against Infantino’s predecessor Sepp Blatter when he was FA chairman, claimed that the FIFA plan “stinks” and England should "have to have the guts” to boycott the World Cup.

Mark Palios, the former FA chief executive, said: “UEFA have a real card to play, and that is if they don’t turn up at the next World Cup that’s going to be an absolute financial disaster for FIFA.”

‌



He added: “If you don’t have Spain, France, England, Germany there, then it’s not going to be anything like the spectacle that it normally is. That’s the major card they have to play and I hope they do play that.”

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan is seen as a money grab (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

The divide between UEFA and FIFA is already well established with Aleksander Ceferin and Infantino not seeing eye-to-eye, so much so that Ceferin didn't attend the World Cup. Europe's governing body were outspoken about some of the decisions taken in the World Cup, including the Folarin Balogun red card saga.

‌



Infantino has attempted to sell his plan and claimed on Wednesday: "It is an opportunity but not an obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

The FIFA boss also tried to sweeten supporters by suggesting: "Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries."

Sports.title: UEFA to boycott FIFA tournaments if World Cup sell-off goes ahead
Sports.content:
UEFA will boycott FIFA tournaments if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with his proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup.

The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of all UEFA's 55 member associations on Thursday afternoon.

The boycott should effectively kill off Infantino's proposal as investors would be unlikely to put money into tournaments without European teams.

The first major tournament UEFA can boycott is the 2027 Women's World Cup, which starts on June 24 next year.

More to follow...

What happens to Infantino if plans collapse?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol breaks down whether Gianni Infantino will succeed with his plan to 'sell-off' the World Cup.

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"It's shocking how nothing is shocking any more. I should be surprised but I'm not surprised at all. I've just come back from the World Cup. According to FIFA, it was the most successful World Cup ever. They made more money than they know what to do with. Fans were paying outrageous prices for tickets.

"Gianni Infantino and those close to him have looked at this and said, 'this is the future'. One way to make sure you have more tournaments like the one you've just had is to set up a subsidiary of FIFA that will look after FIFA's tournaments and to invite private investors to invest in that company.

"In the short term, there's going to be a big pot of money potentially available for the 211 member associations of FIFA.

"The big question is, are they going to accept what Infantino is proposing? What happens to Infantino if these plans collapse? Are we seeing a tipping point on the horizon where a lot of people in football are saying they don't like the way Infantino has been running football?

"I think there is such a groundswell of opposition to these plans that if I had to put money on it, I think they won't succeed. It reminds me of what happened to the European Super League where plans came out, there was outrage and pretty quickly the plans didn't come to fruition.

"Infantino knows everyone has got a price. FIFA have written to all 211 member associations and have said you have until September 19 to accept this plan. If you do, there is going to be a pot of £7.5bn for us to share. If you don't, that pot will drop from £7.5bn to £2bn.

"How many of these member associations are going to turn down that money?"
