Sports.title: Carra: Liverpool don't need Barcola - they need to replace Salah!
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool do not need to buy Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain - urging his former club to focus on securing a replacement for Mohamed Salah on the right wing.

Sky Sports News has reported that Liverpool are preparing an opening offer for the France international forward - who is also wanted by Arsenal and, according to some sources, is valued at £128.5m by the European champions.

However with Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and new signing Victor Munoz as Liverpool's left wing options, Carragher believes Liverpool are stockpiling in one position - and argues there is no one to replace the departed Salah on the opposite flank.

"He's a great player, there's no doubt about that - I'd love to get Barcola at Liverpool," Carragher told Sky Sports News. "But he's a left winger for me.

"Liverpool's big thing that stands out like a sore thumb right now is replacing Mo Salah, a right winger. And I don't think Liverpool have got anybody really in the squad who looks fully comfortable playing right wing.

Image: Bradley Barcola's minutes by position for PSG in the Champions League

"They probably have at least four players in the squad before Barcola joins, if he joins, who could play on the left-hand side comfortably.

"Now, I'm not saying any of those players are better than Barcola. But in terms of the balance of the squad, it's not the position Liverpool need right now. They need a right winger.

"But if you're saying to me, do I want Barcola to come and Liverpool are going to sign a right winger as well? I'll be absolutely delighted because players would have to move on. Of course they would.

"But right now, I felt this summer would be about replacing Mo Salah. Barcola doesn't replace Mo Salah."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Karembeu assess potential destinations for Bradley Barcola after rumours linking the PSG star with a switch to Arsenal and Liverpool

Could Barcola block the path of Ngumoha?

It was also put to Carragher that signing Barcola, who turns 24 in September, could block the path of exciting young winger Ngumoha.

The teenage winger turns 18 in August and had a breakout season last term, scoring twice in 19 Premier League appearances.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp recounts a time when he saw Rio Ngumoha train at his house and was staggered by how fast his feet were, praising the 17 year-old's work ethic as well as his natural talent

Asked if Ngumoha's development could be stalled by Liverpool signing Barcola, Carragher replied: "That is a thought.

"Rio's a young lad, he's really good. I think he's going to kick on from where he did last season. But that is a point: you're buying a really young player for a lot of money in Barcola, who's better than Rio Ngumoha right now.

"But you think eventually in the next year or two, Rio would want to be playing week in, week out for Liverpool. And that's up to him to prove it.

"So when you pay that type of money for a young player in his position, it does leave you scratching your head a little bit.

"There's talk that Rio Ngumoha could play on the right and get some minutes there. As a young player, that's fine, playing on both sides. But I think his position is the left-right now.

"And the reason I'm a little bit confused with Barcola is because last season, when Liverpool sold Luis Diaz, the noise was coming from the club was: we're not buying a left winger because we've got Gakpo - and we also don't want to block the path of Rio Ngumoha.

"And you think, well, OK. I understand that to a certain extent.

"But Rio is now 12 months on. He's proven that he looks a tasty player. And you think Liverpool might have a player there for the future. Yet 12 months on, Liverpool are going to break the bank for someone in that position. When 12 months earlier they said they didn't want to block Rio's path.

"So there are a few things with Liverpool transfer-wise at the moment where I'm still scratching my head a little bit.

"But if they go out and get a player for the right wing, bring Barcola in and then sell a couple of the wide players that they have on the books right now, I think that'd be fantastic."

Sports.title: Britain's Allen becomes first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing
Sports.content:
Decorated British amateur Kayla Allen will make her professional debut in London in September after becoming the first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing.

The 21-year-old Londoner will campaign as a lightweight and make her first professional appearance on September 26, live on Sky Sports, at the Copper Box Arena on the undercard of ZUFFA BOXING 11, headlined by heavyweight star Johnny Fisher.

Allen's deal with Zuffa Boxing marks the latest step in a remarkable rise to a boxing career that began when she first put on a pair of gloves less than five years ago.

"I'm delighted to have signed with Zuffa Boxing as their first female athlete," Allen said.

"I feel honoured to be in this position. With the backing of Zuffa and Sky Sports, I can become a big star on both sides of the Atlantic.

"I appreciate my team for believing in me and securing this landmark deal. I'll be bringing the heat in the ring, and my fans will bring the noise on September 26."

Allen's ascent to becoming one of Britain's most accomplished young amateurs started when she set up a heavy bag in her garden and began learning the craft by watching videos of Floyd Mayweather Jr. and Mike Tyson.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Heavyweight contender Johnny Fisher has signed for Zuffa and will fight live on Sky Sports at Copper Box Arena on September 26

After a short stint on the white-collar circuit, Allen joined GB Boxing and reached the Senior Elite finals in her first year as an amateur.

She captured gold at many of Europe's most prestigious tournaments, including the 2024 Haringey Box Cup and the 2025 Senior Elite Championships.

Allen concluded her amateur career with triumphs at the 2025 European U23 Championships and 2026 Boxam Tournament in La Nucia, Spain. She will begin her professional career under the guidance of long-time trainer Alex Leo.

Watch Kayla Allen's professional debut on the undercard of Johnny Fisher's next fight at London's Copper Box Arena, on Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports. Get Sky Sports or stream boxing with no contract.

Sports.title: 'Dream come true' - Makhanya seals Rangers move from MLS
Sports.content:
Rangers have completed the signing of centre-back Olwethu Makhanya from Philadelphia Union in a deal worth around £3m.

The 22-year-old is the club's eighth summer arrival, having signed a four-year contract, with Rangers holding the option of extending that deal by a further 12 months.

Sky Sports News revealed earlier this month the South Africa international - who had played 53 times for the MLS club - was of interest to Ibrox chiefs this summer.

Rangers get their Scottish Premiership campaign underway at Dundee United on Friday, live on Sky Sports.

Speaking after joining Rangers, he said: "I can't even explain how I am feeling right now, it is honestly a big honour and a huge blessing for me to joins such a big club with so much history. I can't wait to get started.

"For me, it has always been a dream to play football in Europe, ever since I was a kid, so to be here is a dream come true."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Derek McInnes sets out his targets for his first season as Rangers manager ahead of their Scottish Premiership opener at Dundee United, live on Sky Sports

Manager Derek McInnes commented: "We're really pleased to bring Olwethu to the club. He's a player we have watched closely, and we feel he has all the attributes to make a real impact here, while also continuing to develop his game.

"For someone so young, he's already gained experience in different environments. He is a strong, physical and confident defender, and I look forward to seeing him settle into the squad and show what he is capable of as a Rangers player."

Who else could join Rangers?

Rangers have now signed eight players this summer, with Vanja Dragojevic, Lawrence Shankland, Cammy Devlin, Ben Godfrey, Ross McCrorie, Dan Neil and Ivor Pandur joining before Makhanya.

However, they are now working on adding an attacking option as boss McInnes searches for more creativity.

Sky Sports News revealed Coventry City winger Jahnoah Markelo is one option under consideration.

The Ibrox side will also look to add more defensive options too, with the likes of John Souttar among the players who could leave the club.

Sports.title: Scottish Rugby chief sacked following investigation into conduct
Sports.content:
Scottish Rugby has sacked chief executive Alex Williamson following an independent investigation into his conduct.

Williamson began work at Murrayfield in early 2025 after being appointed successor to Mark Dodson the previous September.

He was placed on extended leave in May this year, with Scottish Rugby giving no details at the time about the reasons behind the decision.

Chairman of Scottish Rugby Limited, John McGuigan, said in a statement: "The board of Scottish Rugby has today dismissed Alex Williamson from his position as chief executive with immediate effect.

"His dismissal follows the conclusion of an independent investigation into matters that were brought to the board's attention earlier this year.

"In light of the investigation findings, the board of Scottish Rugby concluded that the CEO's conduct had fallen significantly below the standards we set as an organisation."

Williamson began work at Murrayfield in early 2025 after being appointed successor to Mark Dodson the previous September.

The SRU announced on May 23 this year that Williamson was on a "period of extended leave" but gave no details at the time about the reasons behind the development.

Chief financial officer David White will act as chief executive on an interim basis while the recruitment process for a new chief executive takes place.

Sports.title: Real Madrid expected to make offer for Rodri
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are expected to make an offer for Manchester City midfielder Rodri.

Real are believed to have made initial contact with City over signing Spain's World Cup-winning captain, Sky Sports News understands.

The Spanish giants are believed to be willing to pay in the region of £43m-£51m (€50m-€60m), given he has one year left on his contract.

City do not want to sell Rodri, however, and are hoping instead to agree a new long-term contract with their talismanic midfielder.

Rodri had successful back surgery on Monday and is currently recovering. He is expected to miss the Community Shield and the opening Premier League fixture of the season as a result.

City want him to lead the team into the new Enzo Maresca era - but Real are now ready to make their move. Upon his re-election as Real president, Florentino Perez was criticised for the club having a lack of representation in the Spain national team.

They have already signed Marc Cucurella from Chelsea this summer, and everyone at Real is thought to be on board with a move for Rodri next.

City are believed to progressing with a deal for Lille and Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Carra: Don't sell Rodri for £40-50m!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher urges Manchester City to keep midfielder Rodri for the final season of his contract rather than sell him in this transfer window

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"£40-50m? If you're Manchester City, what's the point in selling them? You might as well just keep them for the extra year.

"He's as good as anybody in that position in the Premier League, probably the best. Seeing what he was like in the World Cup, it was like he was back to his best.

"I thought the second half of the season him and Bernardo Silva were fantastic and almost took Manchester City to the title.

"So, if I was the manager of Manchester City, I'd be keeping Rodri at that price. It'd have to be something really special to want me to lose arguably the best midfield player in world football.

"I think it'd be really tough for them to win the Premier League without Rodri, even though they've got a lot of midfielders. He's the best, even though they've brought Elliot Anderson, who is one who I'm sure will learn off Rodri.

"And for me, I'd see those two as a pair. I see Elliot Anderson as almost the replacement for Bernardo Silva, who's gone to Real Madrid. So, I think that'd be a big hole. It'd be really difficult to fill.

"When Liverpool won the title under Arne Slot, Rodri got an injury in that season very early on, which helped Liverpool and was to the detriment of Manchester City. So if I was Manchester City, I'd be keeping him and letting him go on a free.

"City paid £60m for him. If they're getting £40m back now, what can they do with that type of money? Not a lot, really. So, I'd rather keep him."

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

Massive. Despite his age, and recent injury record, Rodri remains the most complete central midfielder to have operated in the Premier League over the past five years. "The best midfielder in the world by far," maintains Pep Guardiola.

Under Guardiola, City's in-play strategy revolved entirely around him, always impressing with his use of the ball and ability to receive in tight situations. He set the tempo for his team and controlled games as a result, doing the same for triumphant Spain this summer.

There is no current player who can condition a game like Rodri, and it is no coincidence City failed to retain their Premier League crown in the two seasons he was injury-plagued.

So, how is he replaced?

In short, he isn't.

But in Anderson City have got a surrogate of sorts. The England international might not yet be the dictator Rodri is but he can evolve to become something close. As a box-to-box midfielder, the 23-year-old is putting up numbers that at least mean he is comparable.

Sports.title: Reinvigorate Root and fix culture: What's in new Test coach Fleming's in-tray?
Sports.content:
England have announced the appointment of Stephen Fleming as coach of the men's Test team and he will take over after the three-Test series against Pakistan. We take a look at the jobs on his to-do list ahead of a bumper year…

Reinvigorate Root

Ben Stokes' shock - and extravagant, considering it came at 3.25pm while he was midway through a bowling spell - retirement from international cricket meant England needed a captain to lead them post-Bazball.

Enter Joe Root. The former skipper - who has captained the most all-time England Tests with 65 - is set to take the mantle for a second time after a first five-year stint as captain between 2017 and 2022.

Fleming talked of "bedding in the gains" made by Stokes and Brendon McCullum in his upcoming tenure, and clearly he and the ECB have decided that tried-and-trusted Root - rather than white-ball captain and Test vice-captain Harry Brook - is the man to do just that.

Image: Joe Root has been reappointed as captain, having done it in 65 Tests previously

Root's captaincy, though, is not without its drawbacks. He gave it up after five years in charge having won one Test in his last 17, and told Sky Sports in 2022 that the role had started to have "an unhealthy effect on the rest of my life".

His recent outing as interim Test captain in the absence of Stokes did not do much to reassure doubters. England were subjected to a drubbing, losing the second Test against New Zealand by 253 runs at The Oval in uninspiring fashion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Butcher questioned the decision to name Root as captain

"Joe was completely wrung out at the end of his time as captain for five years," former England batter Mark Butcher told Sky Sports News. "The best thing that happened to him and his game was not being captain any more.

"I think it's a retrograde step for the team... I just don't think it's the best move for him to be captain at this time or at any other moment in time actually."

Fleming's first task, then, has to be readying his veteran leader for the daunting task of a winter tour of South Africa and then the home Ashes next summer.

Develop unfinished-product Brook

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the fifth T20 international between England and India in Southampton as the hosts romped to a 4-0 series win

The new coach and the powers that be have clearly decided Brook is not ready for such a consuming role. He was overlooked as stand-in leader for the Oval Test against New Zealand after the Stokes nightclub saga, having become embroiled in a nightclub drama of his own in New Zealand before an ODI last winter.

Brook, though, reignited conversations after guiding England to a 4-0 T20 series win over India that moved them top of the T20I rankings and a 2-1 ODI series victory over the same opponents. He appears to have a pretty sharp cricketing mind a lot of the time - but, according to Fleming, he needs more time before taking on the red-ball captaincy.

"I'm also excited to work with Harry Brook," Fleming said. "The best players are never finished products, and helping Harry continue to develop his extraordinary talent and his leadership will be an important part of this journey."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Root's 99 not out guided England to a four-wicket win over India in the second ODI

Root's reinstatement has ended concerns over whether Brook could captain in all three forms amid such a packed fixture schedule, and will give the white-ball captain more time to develop his leadership and focus on the upcoming 50-over World Cup in 2027.

Root, though, turns 36 in December, and his appointment will most likely solely focus on the bumper year of Test cricket ahead - as it feels difficult to imagine the skipper leading the team much beyond that.

With Brook seemingly the captain-in-waiting, it is perhaps just as incumbent on Fleming to help bring on future leaders as to support the one he has put in place now.

Work with white-ball coach McCullum

Image: Brendon McCullum has been succeeded by Fleming as England Test coach

While splitting the roles between red and white-ball cricket will allow complete focus on one format for each coach - and therefore reduce the risk of burnout - England's two head honchos will need a strong relationship for it to work.

Fleming and McCullum certainly have that. The two played alongside each other for six years for New Zealand - with McCullum making his Test debut under Fleming's captaincy - and they were even investors in a business together, cricHQ.

McCullum has said that "robust" conversations will take place with the Test coach in order to "achieve harmony and success" for English cricket, which can probably be read along the lines of: "I won't be asset stripped."

That harmony feels significantly easier to maintain with two coaches so familiar with each other already.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McCullum speaks on what it will be like working with a new Test coach for England as well as the future of the white-ball side

Test cricket, with that home Ashes in a year's time, is clearly the priority, hence why McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties following the malaise he oversaw.

But Fleming will not want that to damage England's excellent T20 form or the objective of fixing an ODI side languishing eighth in the rankings and winning the 2027 50-over World Cup.

England fans crave success on all fronts - there has been no global white-ball trophy since 2022, no Ashes win since 2015 - and the coaches must align to make that possible.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following England's Test series defeat to New Zealand, Nasser Hussain gave a scathing review of McCullum's Test-series record

Fix the boozing and off-field indiscipline

England have had more drink-related incidents than their Test side has had wins of late, with Brook's scrap with a bouncer in New Zealand, Ben Duckett seemingly intoxicated during a pilloried beach break in Noosa between Ashes Tests, and then Stokes and Gus Atkinson's curfew-breaking, headline-making trip to a Chelsea nightspot.

How clear the curfew was remains, well, unclear and that is another black mark that can be labelled against this team: lack of attention to detail.

We saw that in their Ashes preparation, with just one warm-up game prior to the Perth Test - and not a particularly useful one at that, in that it was played on a docile surface at Lilac Hill that in no way matched the bouncy deck they would come up against at Optus Stadium. And we all know what happened there…

Image: Ben Stokes is now concentrating on playing for Durham

Batters out driving on the up ad nauseum as England threw away a golden position. Now-interim coach Marcus Trescothick would later say there were no discussions about playing those shots on that surface. Really?!

"There's been a number of times now that we've let ourselves down" incoming captain Root said after England's latest escapade.

"We have to learn from those mistakes and understand that we shouldn't be putting ourselves in those situations."

The ECB issued new additional player behaviour guidelines in July ahead of the three-Test series against Pakistan - it is now up to Fleming and Root to make sure they are followed far better than under Stokes and McCullum.

Replace Stokes and nail down best XI

Image: Rehan Ahmed is an option as England's Test all-rounder

Stokes' departure - unless he can be lured back - not only deprives England of a talismanic captain but also a gun all-rounder, even if his batting form tapered off at the back end of his Test career with just one hundred since the 2023 Ashes.

There is no easy fix here, although Sam Curran is a seam-bowling all-rounder option - his left-arm angle may be useful - while Rehan Ahmed offers a spin-bowling one. Leg-spinner Ahmed's inclusion at No 7 could allow England to play four frontline quicks.

Most of the batting spots look locked in: Bethell at No 3, Root at No 4, Brook at No 5 and possibly, after a timely ton versus New Zealand, Duckett as one opener. Duckett's top-order accomplice is maybe not so certain with Emilio Gay hitting two fifties against the Kiwis but tailing off thereafter. Other county openers will feel they have a chance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes took a wicket moments after announcing his retirement from international cricket

The same will apply for spinners with the two men who made Shoaib Bashir their pet project, Stokes and McCullum, no longer around. Bashir has potential, no doubt, but the new Test coach may want someone with more tangible stats behind them. Jack Leach, perhaps?

Jamie Smith could also be sweating on his spot as wicketkeeper-batter. After a lean Ashes, he did not fare outstandingly against New Zealand, albeit his replacement at The Oval while he was on paternity leave, James Rew, toiled with bat and gloves during a sobering debut.

Win matches and big series

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McCullum reveals what his ambitions were with Bazball after becoming Test coach in 2022

Of all the objectives on the coach's to-do list, this is right at the top of it.

The end of the Bazball era saw just three wins from the final 12 matches, while the whole of the Bazball era saw no series victories over Australia and India - the contests on which England are judged - with 2-2 draws at home to those sides and 4-1 batterings away.

Fleming should not - and most likely will not - abandon every Bazball principle. Attacking, in-your-face cricket got England into a number of match-winning positions over the last four years - only for the players to get too amped up and then chuck those positions away by not reining themselves in. See Lord's 2023, Rajkot 2024 and Perth 2025 as prime examples.

The task is to cut out the brainless bits and make sure refinement and responsibility come when games are in the palm of England's hands, as while English fans obviously enjoy entertaining cricket, they love winning cricket even more.

And they love winning against Australia more than anything. That opportunity arises again next summer, which makes Fleming's appointment crucial.

Sports.title: Fifa’s sales pitch revealed: more tournaments, more debt … but no mention of women’s game
Sports.content:
Fifa’s sales pitch to persuade members to approve the sale of the World Cup’s commercial rights clearly states that their plans for financial growth will be achieved by staging more tournaments, having higher ticket prices and debt financing.

A 25-page sales deck titled “Fifa Forward Enterprise Member Materials”, which has been seen by the Guardian, makes the case for the creation of a new company to run Fifa’s commercial operations, 20% of which would be sold to Joshua Kushner, a US investor who is the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

The prospectus has been produced by JP Morgan, the US bank that was also behind the failed European Super League breakaway five years ago.

In addition to the previously reported $20m (£15m) sign-up payment Fifa has offered to all 211 member associations, which could be made available as soon as next January, the document projects that the four-year Fifa Forward payments would increase to $24m for each member by the 2035-39 cycle.

JP Morgan makes clear in the sales deck that such growth will come from “a growing tournament portfolio”, “third party sources of capital and debt financing”, and prioritising “high yield” partnerships and events.

There is also a reference to more than doubling the number of global tournaments held each year, from 200 to 450, which if followed through would put a huge strain on player workload.

Staging the World Cup more frequently would be most obvious way of raising revenue, with Gianni Infantino having previously proposed making it a biennial tournament five years ago.

The bank also raises the prospect of TV coverage of the biggest events such as the World Cup being sold to subscription channels or streamers, by referring to a plan to “expand and optimize media rights monetization”.

JP Morgan claims that Fifa is “undermonetized” but significantly makes comparisons with other sports leagues with the revenue figures based on club or franchise earnings, rather than with comparable governing bodies.

Fifa’s stated annual revenue of $3.6bn therefore compares unfavourably with the NFL’s compared revenue of $21.2bn, Major League Baseball’s $13.1bn and the NBA’s $12.5bn.

The document was sent to all 211 member associations on Wednesday night and immediately provoked a strong reaction.

One senior figure queried why Fifa, which has cash reserves of around $4bn and accumulated revenues of $15bn over the current four-year cycle, would need to take on debt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another highlighted the odd comparison of a world governing body with private, member-run leagues, while JP Morgan’s proposed timeline for completing the deal was also questioned.

According to the document “Investors will be given access to a term sheet and select materials” in August before a vote of Fifa members has taken place.

Significantly there is little mention of the investor group elsewhere in the prospect, with reference to their identity, their projected returns or exit terms.

There is one more major omission in the document, as there is not a single mention of women’s football anywhere across the 25 pages.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe leaves Newcastle United with Matthias Jaissle set to replace him
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left Newcastle after losing control of transfers and is set to be replaced by the German coach Matthias Jaissle, who is in charge of the Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli.

Although the timing of Howe’s abrupt departure following almost five years in charge at St James’ Park is unexpected, his position had been uncertain for some time. He is understood to have told Newcastle’s Saudi Arabian owners he wanted to leave more than a fortnight ago and the parting is said to be “amicable”.

Sources have suggested the 48-year-old told directors he was utterly drained and wanted to take a break from football following a transformative Tyneside tenure that saw Newcastle win the League Cup in 2025 and twice qualify for the Champions League.

In recent months Howe has become disillusioned after seeing his previously strong power-base and ability to dictate transfer policy diminished significantly. Already this summer Ross Wilson, the third sporting director of his managerial tenure, has presided over the sale of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively. A year ago the team’s key striker Alexander Isak departed for Liverpool.

Quick Guide Howe's highs and lows at Newcastle Show 2021-22: The firefighter After taking over from Steve Bruce in November 2021, Eddie Howe gets strong backing in the January transfer window and guides Newcastle to an 11th-place finish. A run of six straight wins at home sees the Magpies become the first team in Premier League history to avoid relegation after failing to win any of their first 14 games.

2022-23: Return to Europe Alexander Isak arrives for big money in the summer, but it is mostly existing players like Callum Wilson and Miguel Almirón who power Howe's side to the League Cup final, which ends in defeat to Manchester United. Newcastle respond well, earning a fourth-place finish to qualify for the Champions League. 2023-24: Injuries bite Howe's training methods are called into doubt as Newcastle finish bottom of their Champions League group and struggle with injuries all season. They also lose £55m signing Sandro Tonali to a betting ban. A late run earns seventh spot but European hopes are dashed as Manchester United stun City in the FA Cup final. 2024-25: League Cup triumph A brilliant, Dan Burn-inspired win over Liverpool at Wembley sees Howe lift the League Cup (pictured) and finally end Newcastle's long trophy drought. With Isak banging in 23 Premier League goals, the Toon secure a fifth-place finish, which is good enough to earn Champions League qualification once again. 2025-26: The ghost of Isak A summer-long saga over the sale of Isak to Liverpool scuppers plans for Howe's fourth full season in charge. The fans turn on wantaway Anthony Gordon midway through a campaign that is all but ended by a humiliating 7-2 defeat at Barcelona in March. Howe's final five months in charge feature 14 defeats across all competitions as Newcastle slump to 12th in the Premier League. Tom Bassam Photograph: Danny Lawson/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Not that Howe gave any indication of the events about to unfold when he spoke to reporters following Wednesday night’s 4-1 pre-season friendly defeat at Bristol City. “Every day as Newcastle manager is a great day for me,” he said. “I absolutely love the football club and that will never change. There has been a lot of change at the football club and potentially more to come. [But] I think there’s always reasons to be optimistic. I believe great things are possible every season. I see no reason for it be any different this year.”

On Thursday morning the Newcastle hierarchy’s negotiations with Jaissle were said to be at an advanced stage and the club’s players had a day off interrupted by news that that there would be a change of manager. Given that Al-Ahli are also owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Jaissle’s split from his club is unlikely to prove problematic.

The 38-year-old had a brief playing career as a defender with Hoffenheim and has been in charge of Al-Ahli since 2023, presiding over 90 wins, 25 draws and 23 defeats. Along the way he has won a Saudi Super Cup and two Asian Champions Leagues. In his first major head coaching role, at RB Salzburg, he won two league titles and the Austrian Cup in two seasons.

After finishing a disappointing 12th in the Premier League last season some Newcastle fans were calling for Howe’s dismissal but the former Bournemouth manager appeared to have convinced PIF to offer him another chance during a high level summit meeting at a Northumberland country house hotel in April. He is understood to have reiterated his commitment to the job after returning from holiday in June but subsequently became disenchanted by the events of a turbulent summer. Quite apart from the exits of Gordon and Tonali it has featured doubt surrounding the future of the Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimarães who is coveted by Arsenal.

At Bristol City on Wednesday night, Howe admitted he had “lost control” of transfers and did not know if Guimarães would board the team’s flight to South east Spain ahead of a training Camp at La Manga on Friday.

While Guimarães is understood to have told Newcastle he wants to join Arsenal this summer, Howe had developed increasing reservations about a new, PIF approved, policy of signing largely young players with high resale potential priced, broadly, in the £20m-£40m bracket. With Newcastle operating under a Uefa settlement agreement, Wilson believes it is the best way to remain within football’s spending rules.

View image in fullscreen Eddie Howe oversaw a 4-1 friendly defeat to Bristol City on Wednesday, in what proved to be his final game in charge. Photograph: David Davies/PA

So far this summer the sporting director has recruited four promising yet inexperienced players aged 20 or under in Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Touré, Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur. Howe feared expectations had been raised earlier this year when his chief executive David Hopkinson claimed he wanted Newcastle to “be in the conversation” about the identity of the best clubs in the world by 2030. Howe told friends things “no longer felt right.”

Although Howe acquired a number of critics as results, increasingly, disappointed last season, he will long be remembered with affection and gratitude at St James’ Park. After succeeding Steve Bruce as manager in November 2021 he led Newcastle to two Carabao Cup finals and in winning the second - against Liverpool - last year secured the club’s first significant domestic silverware for 70 years.

With his assistant, Jason Tindall, also expected to leave, the squad are likely to be placed under the caretaker charge of first team coach, Graeme Jones, for the trip to La Manga.

The club hope that Jaissle will soon join them. With the former Nottingham Forest manager Vítor Pereira poised to replace him at Al-Ahli, the expectation is that the German will take the helm well before ­Newcastle’s training camp concludes with a friendly game at Valencia on Saturday 8 August.Alan Shearer has been taken aback by the change’s timeline. “I’m very, very surprised,” said the club’s former captain and manager. “It’s strange timing with three weeks to go until the new season. I don’t know what’s gone on but I’m led to believe it was Eddie’s decision to leave. He did a wonderful job so it’s a huge thank you to Eddie.”

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott revels in ‘second chance’ at Liverpool and has no regrets over Aston Villa loan
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott believes he has been given “a second chance” at Liverpool and denied his ill-fated loan to Aston Villa was a lost year in his career.

Elliott joined Villa on a season-long loan last September with an obligation for them to buy the midfielder for £35m once he made 10 appearances for the club. However, Elliott featured only nine times, playing 277 minutes in total, with Unai Emery and Villa unconvinced over completing the deal. Having made an 89th-minute substitute appearance for Liverpool at Newcastle in August, the 23-year-old was unable to sign for a third club in a single season.

Elliott has featured in both of Liverpool’s pre-season wins under Andoni Iraola in the United States. While non-committal about his long-term future – Sunday’s opponents Leeds have been linked – Elliott spoke positively about his time at Villa, the first time he has discussed last season’s issues, and claimed he could yet feature in Iraola’s plans.

“Everyone knows how much I love the club so the feeling never goes of putting the shirt back on, representing the club, and fulfilling your childhood dream,” said Elliott, a boyhood Liverpool fan. “But truthfully, yes [I felt it would never happen again], because I wanted a new challenge. I wanted to explore something, come out of my comfort zone, and I thought that would take me on as a player. Unfortunately, it didn’t work out, but the way I see it is it’s kind of a second chance, especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in.

“It’s another chance to impress and hopefully get in their good books. But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best. I had a lot of love for them and they treated me very well. I’m here now, and I’m trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad.”

Elliott insists he harbours “no hard feelings” towards Villa. The Liverpool player was named player of the tournament at the European Under-21s Championship in the summer of 2025 and was touted as a possible member of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad before his career stalled in the Midlands. But he insists: “I wouldn’t say it was a lost year because, at the end of it, I won the Europa League. To have that on my CV is incredible, especially with Villa. I saw with my own eyes how much it meant for them and I wouldn’t say it’s a lost year when you achieved something like that, because that’s selfish.

“It was a situation I couldn’t control. It was just a case of accepting it, and just trying to get my head clear and get myself in the best position to come back here, and I tried as hard as I could. I still feel like I can get better and I’m working as hard as I can to do that.”

Elliott admits Emery discussed his reasoning several times and that enabled him to handle the frustration of being sidelined for the majority of the season. “He explained very, very clearly and a fair few times. The whole club were very apologetic about the situation and, ultimately, it was a situation that I couldn’t control,” Elliott said. “But I knew 100% what the case was. It was like, ‘Ok, I can get over it, I know what the situation is now’.

“It was just about me handling it and showing my professionalism. I’m not that kind of guy who wanted to kick up a fuss and cause problems, because no one really deserves that. It’s just part of football and it was a learning curve for me and an opportunity that I hope I don’t experience again. But it’s a situation where I know I’ve been able to get through it.

“I’m really happy to be back and putting a Liverpool shirt on again. Playing at Liverpool, there’s no better feeling.”

Sports.title: France defender Maxence Lacroix joins ‘beautiful club’ Chelsea from Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Maxence Lacroix has joined Chelsea from Crystal Palace to become the club’s fifth signing of the summer so far. The France international, who won the FA Cup and Conference League with Palace, has been the Blues’ main defensive target of the window.

Lacroix, 26, signs a six-year deal with Xabi Alonso’s side. “I am really happy to be part of this beautiful club,” said Lacroix, who played three times for France at the World Cup, including in their 6-4 bronze medal match defeat to England.

“Everyone knows the legend of Chelsea, its tradition of winning, and to be a part of that is a proud moment. I think it’s the best move for me because it’s the best club in the world. When I spoke with the manager, I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

“We want to win. When you see the quality of the players here, everything we have around the club, it’s something that we can achieve. The ambition is to lift trophies, and I can’t wait to contribute.”

Chelsea had been looking to add experience to their back line having missed out on Rennes’ Jeremy Jacquet in January, with the player opting to join Liverpool. Levi Colwill, who is considered to be a key part of the club’s long-term plans, missed almost all of last season with an anterior cruciate ligament injury, with Wesley Fofana and Trevoh Chalobah forming the central-defensive partnership for much of the campaign.

After a dismal season that saw the club finish 10th, the club’s hierarchy has acknowledged a change in recruitment policy is needed, with a refocusing away from young, inexperienced players towards ones that can help the team compete for the title.

Lacroix, who made 55 appearances last season for Palace, has been one of the league’s most consistent defenders since moving to Selhurst Park from Wolfsburg in 2024.

The Blues confirmed the club-record arrival of Aston Villa forward Morgan Rogers last week, and have also added Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, striker Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg and Sporting Lisbon’s Geovany Quenda.

Chelsea also look set to sign Brighton’s Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson after his contract with Brentford was terminated.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership returns with McInnes adding new twist to Old Firm rivalry
Sports.content:
Only residents of cloud cuckoo land can hold the firm belief of Scottish football emerging promptly from a summer of discontent. The onset of a new domestic season, ordinarily a cause for excitement, instead gives reason to ponder the grim realities of what came before.

That it is unsurprising there has been no detailed explanation or plan from the Scottish Football Association following a lamentable World Cup does not prevent the scenario from being so deflating. Mike Mulraney, the president, was last seen peeking out from the crowd behind Gianni Infantino and the US president at Trump Tower. Ian Maxwell, the Scottish FA’s chief executive, bemoaned “hysterical commentary” around his country’s World Cup performance during a brief media appearance after Steve Clarke had resigned. These executives had all-but spurted with laughter when it was suggested handing Clarke a four-year contract immediately before Scotland set sail for the United States was perhaps a needless dalliance with risk.

Perhaps Mulraney and Maxwell are too engrossed in the sourcing of Clarke’s replacement to speak out on the overall state of the national sport. It is only fair to give them the opportunity to appoint a coach who can oversee much-needed transition in a geriatric Scotland squad. The nation’s leading clubs have been moot on a big picture they wilfully ignore but was exposed at a World Cup. The problem is that lingering and legitimate anger over Scotland’s showing on the biggest stage – despite all rationale behind it – mirrors so much broader sentiment as the Premiership returns. This has scope to be a troublesome, toxic campaign.

Celtic’s supporters remain irate at the custodians of their club, whom they perceive as complacent and out of touch. In Derek McInnes, Rangers have a new manager who is deeply unpopular on the other side of the city. Nobody should underestimate the lingering resentment that exists among followers of Hearts over the way the campaign of 2025-26 concluded. The most reprehensible element of that arrived on 11 June, when the Scottish Professional Football League published the outcome of a disciplinary process into the pitch invasion which forced the ending of Celtic’s title-clinching clash against the Edinburgh club.

View image in fullscreen Celtic fans run on to the pitch after their team went 3-1 up against Hearts in the title-deciding game. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Snuggled in alongside wrist tickles for Hamilton Academical, Inverness and Stenhousemuir was a meagre fine for Celtic and a suspended, paltry ticket reduction. Rangers fans, who need little encouragement to rail against officialdom, were subdued until McInnes was slapped with a touchline ban for comments made against a refereeing decision. Rangers have criticised elements of an independent report into the chaos which followed their March Scottish Cup loss to Celtic. Motherwell are speaking with lawyers due to objection to a Scottish FA fine for a video posted on social media. A 2-0 European qualifying first-leg defeat in Kosovo last week was rightly sufficient to send Hibs fanatics into the internet’s version of orbit. Such results stopped being a shock long ago.

Certain clubs do actually have reasons to be cheerful. Celtic’s signing of Kasper Høgh for a club-record fee not only demonstrated the kind of fiscal muscle-flexing that supporters wish happened more often but provided the most intriguing transfer arrival of the close season. Scepticism exists over the ability of players to perform outside the perennially successful environment of Bodø/Glimt. Without such doubts and at a fee which even many Championship clubs would think little of, Høgh would have moved long ago. The 25-year-old, though, has a physical profile and direct style that should succeed in Scotland.

Celtic’s challenge is to replace existing first-team performers – Arne Engels and Alistair Johnston the prime examples – should irresistible bids arrive without posting the kind of net profit that makes balance sheets look more important than trophies. Fans have rightly welcomed the Høgh signing but need more.

Rangers, in contrast to their oldest foes, have burned through extraordinary amounts of cash in recent years while generally watching others lift trophies. This has fuelled rage in and reputational damage from the stands, which an American ownership has curiously opted not to challenge.

In McInnes, Rangers – who kick off the season at Dundee United in Friday’s curtain raiser – have a manager whose knowledge of club and culture looks better placed than most before him in recent years to lay gloves on Celtic. Vanja Dragojevic looks a smart midfield signing from Partizan Belgrade. Rangers need attacking spark yet it should be no surprise that McInnes’s first act was to implement a stronger core. McInnes lacks nothing in motivation or work ethic in the job he has always craved. This version of Rangers should be much improved. Yet on the simple basis of course and distance specialism, Celtic remain the title favourites.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Motherwell’s recent success offers a template for other top-flight clubs to follow. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Nobody linked to Hearts should have been expected to fully process the circumstances which saw them come within minutes of a first title win in 66 years, only for that dream to be snatched away, by now. McInnes’s departure for Rangers, the completely new style implemented by Wouter Vrancken and a palpable raising of expectations all contribute to a period of upheaval. Hearts’ tilt at glory came earlier than anyone could anticipate. The club remains on the minds of people who previously had no interest in the Scottish game. A comprehensive Champions League qualifying defeat to Sturm Graz showed the scale of work Vrancken has ahead of him. Patience, however, would be wise.

Motherwell’s work with and post the management of Jens Berthel Askou proved those below the Premiership’s biggest fish needn’t only cling on for dear life. The football was superb, the attendance figures boosted and a broader market was impressed. Motherwell’s sales of Elijah Just and Elliot Watt for multimillion-pound fees completely justify a club model that thinks outside the box.

St Mirren have clear aspirations of introducing more young players and a more alluring brand of football. Kilmarnock displayed that at the end of last season under Neil McCann. Aberdeen will surely be a stronger force this time under Stephen Robinson. Only one artificial pitch remains in Scotland’s top flight, which provides cause for celebration.

Football remains a Scottish obsession. It is also undeniably a sick patient. The dawning of a fresh season should appeal only if there is a glimpse of fresh thinking.

Sports.title: WSL fixtures: London City Lionesses open 2026-27 season against Manchester United
Sports.content:
Those desperate to see what London City Lionesses will look like with two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas in their ranks do not have to wait long, with the big-spending club kicking off the new Women’s Super League season against Manchester United on Friday 4 September.

The Michelle Kang-owned side welcome United to Hayes Lane in the first game of the 2026-27 season, which will also likely feature goalkeeper Mary Earps, who returns to the WSL for an opener against her former club after leaving Paris Saint-Germain to join London City this summer.

The full fixture list for the new season has been announced, and comes after an extremely complex scheduling process, with WSL Football running more that 1.5 billion scheduling iterations as it juggles the stadium availability and broadcast windows following the announcement of the calendars and fixtures of the Premier League, EFL and men’s National League and men’s FA Cup, women’s FA Cup, Carabao Cup, and men’s and women’s Champions League.

Also on the opening weekend, WSL champions Manchester City, who have added the former Arsenal forward Beth Mead and Chelsea defender Niamh Charles to their ranks, begin their title defence against WSL2 champions Birmingham. The Midlands side were promoted alongside Charlton and Crystal Palace with the top flight expanding to 14 teams for the first time.

Arsenal start their campaign against Brighton, who knocked them out of the FA Cup at the quarter-final stage shortly before they earned a draw in the league against the Gunners that handed Manchester City their first title since 2016.

Elsewhere, Charlton, who earned a playoff win over Leicester to earn their promotion at the expense of the WSL’s bottom-placed side, will play Liverpool at home, Tottenham host West Ham, Chelsea welcome Aston Villa to Stamford Bridge and Crystal Palace mark their return to the WSL against Everton.

In WSL2, Watford will host Burnley at Vicarage Road to kickstart things, while Bristol City, who narrowly missed out on promotion, face Sunderland, Durham play Southampton, Ipswich meet Nottingham Forest, Newcastle host Wolves and Sheffield United tackle relegated Leicester City.

Following the 2025-26 transition season, as the top flight expanded to 14 teams, new relegation and promotion rules begin between the top two divisions for next season. Sports.title: Experimental Liverpool down Wrexham thanks to Rio Ngumoha’s winner
Sports.content:
Liverpool turned the Empire State Building red when launching a new away kit on Tuesday but neither they nor Wrexham could illuminate Yankee Stadium 24 hours later. It was rough in the diamond, although Rio Ngumoha’s deflected goal made it two wins out of two for Andoni Iraola on his first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach.

Ngumoha, a second half substitute who Iraola deployed on the right, satisfied the majority of a 42,204 crowd with a 75th-minute shot that looped in off Wrexham defender Lewis Brunt. Wrexham’s Hollywood co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) were in attendance for what the former had labelled a “punch-me moment” but in truth few blows were traded at the iconic baseball stadium.

Liverpool’s preparations for the second game of pre-season were not exactly smooth, in fairness to Iraola’s team. Their flight from Chicago was cancelled on Tuesday night with players and staff on the tarmac ready to take off. Poor weather conditions in the New York area delayed their arrival until the day of the game, and Liverpool only checked into their Midtown hotel around midday. They were flying back to Chicago straight after the match too.

Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch did not make the trip from Liverpool’s training base despite joining up with the squad following their post-World Cup holidays. The game came too early in their pre-season preparations to be considered. With Joe Gomez injured and Federico Chiesa also absent through illness, Iraola had little choice but to select another young and experimental side. Six of Liverpool’s starting line-up had no Premier League experience whatsoever but at least the emphasis on youth offered the crowd a glimpse of the highly-rated Joshua Abe.

View image in fullscreen Joshua Abe reacts after failing to score at Yankee Stadium. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

Abe, a pacy and prolific right winger, is regarded as one of the brightest prospects in the country and was inundated with offers before committing his future to Liverpool when turning 16 earlier this month. Manchester City, Manchester United and Chelsea were all interested in the Warrington-born England youth international, with deals worth £40,000-a-week reportedly on his table. There was understandable relief inside Anfield when he agreed scholarship terms in June with a three-year professional contract to follow on his 17th birthday next July.

Abe could have marked his first senior Liverpool start with an early goal when released clear of the Wrexham defence by Harvey Elliott. A heavy first touch gave the Wrexham and former Liverpool goalkeeper Danny Ward opportunity to save at the feet of the teenager. Iraola started with a front line of Calum Scanlon, Lewis Koumas and Abe. Koumas went close from distance and had a penalty shout waved away but, aside from a few surging midfield runs by Dominik Szoboszlai, it was a quiet friendly.

Wrexham are further along in their pre-season work – their first competitive game is a week on Friday against Middlesbrough in the Carabao Cup – and it showed as the first half progressed and Phil Parkinson’s team gained a physical edge. Sam Smith and Callum Doyle were unable to trouble Giorgi Mamardashvili with the chances that fell their way.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Abe, Scanlon, Milos Kerkez and Trey Nyoni were replaced at half-time by Ngumoha, Kieran Morrison, Kostas Tsimikas and Curtis Jones respectively. Elliott was presented with a sight of the Wrexham goal by Koumas minutes after the restart but his first-time shot from 20 yards was well saved by Ward. The Wales international also denied Szoboszlai from distance but this was a Liverpool performance – and pre-season friendly – that failed to ignite.

Wrexham substitute Nathan Broadhead almost succeeded with a powerful drive from 25 yards that was pushed away by Mamardashvili. Brunt and Kieffer Moore both had good late chances to equalise but miscued from close range.

Sports.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
Sports.content:
Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta.

As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

The dispute over the islands, which have been ruled by Britain since 1833, is long running and led to a 74-day conflict in 1982, during which more than 900 people – 649 Argentinians and 255 Britons – lost their lives.

Fifa’s disciplinary code ­prohibits “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature” and the banner prompted political debate on both sides of the ­Atlantic. A spokesperson for the then UK prime minister, Keir Starmer, said: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands ­definitely are.” Andrew Giuliani, the head of the White House Fifa taskforce, defended Argentina’s players, saying the US believed in free speech.

The incident was not the first time an Argentina team had expressed such sentiments. In 2014, Fifa fined Argentina £20,000 for a far larger banner held ‌up by players before a friendly with Slovenia in La Plata.

Fifa’s full World Cup charge sheet against the Argentinian Football Association also includes ­“discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches”.

0:18 Ugly scenes as Argentina lose World Cup final – video

Several players are also under investigation in relation to the ­chaotic scenes that followed ­Argentina’s 1-0 extra-time defeat by Spain in the final. As Spain attempted to celebrate, ­altercations broke out across the pitch at New York New Jersey Stadium.

The Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes, who was seen wrestling Spain’s Eric García to the ground, faces three counts of assault under the Fifa disciplinary code, while the defender Nahuel Molina faces two counts of assault (one completed and one attempted) and one count of unsporting behaviour.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The assistant coach, Roberto Ayala, faces one count of assault, and Thiago Almada, an unused substitute in the final, one count of unsporting behaviour. Spain’s Gavi also faces an unsporting behaviour charge.

“In accordance with the Fifa ­disciplinary code, the respondents have now been provided with the opportunity to present their position, following which a decision will be issued by the Fifa disciplinary committee in due course,” said Fifa.

Sports.title: England and fellow UEFA nations set to unanimously BOYCOTT World Cup after FIFA's plans to sell shares to private investors
Sports.content:
England and fellow UEFA nations set to unanimously BOYCOTT World Cup after FIFA's plans to sell shares to private investors

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England and other UEFA nations are prepared to boycott the next World Cup should FIFA go ahead with their plans to sell shares of their flagship tournament.

Europe's governing football body has been staunchly opposed to plans shared this week by FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

FIFA want to create a new company that would generate £3.1billion in private investment for FIFA tournaments, with Joshua Kushner - brother of Jared, Donald Trump’s son-in-law - leading the group of potential investors.

In the wake of this summer's World Cup, Infantino now plans to force FIFA's associations to decide on the proposal by September 19.

But after a crisis meeting held on Thursday, England's Football Associations and fellow UEFA members confirmed that they will boycott FIFA's tournaments, including next summer's Women's World Cup, should the proposal receive the green light.

UEFA's 55 member nations met virtually and their decision could all but kill FIFA's plans due to the sway they hold in international football.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has condemned FIFA's plans to allow private investors a share of the World Cup

Gianni Infantino has been widely criticised for his decision to put the World Cup 'up for sale'

One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: ‘This is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive’.

Issuing a statement in the wake of the decision, UEFA underscored that the 'World Cup is not for sale' and called the secrecy around the plans 'irresponsible and indefensible'.

'UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions,' the statement began. 'UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

'The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

'It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

'National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

'But our opposition goes far beyond process.

'The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

'This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

Football Association chief executive Mark Bullingham came under pressure to take action

'Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

'As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

'Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

'There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

'Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.'

On Wednesday, UEFA had accused FIFA of trying to bribe associations into agreeing with the proposals, which could see them receive up to an additional £15m in revenue.

In another blow to the plan, the president of the Asian Federation Sheikh Salman wrote of his 'great concern and disappointment' in FIFA's decision to prepare the plans without consultation.

CONCACAF, which represents 41 countries in North and Central America and the Caribbean, is another federation which has also expressed early skepticism in the wake of the bombshell plans.

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott opens up on nightmare Aston Villa loan where he was placed into bomb squad by Unai Emery: 'I wouldn't wish that on any player'
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott opens up on nightmare Aston Villa loan where he was placed into bomb squad by Unai Emery: 'I wouldn't wish that on any player'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Harvey Elliott has opened up on his Aston Villa nightmare, saying he wouldn’t wish the tough year he experienced on anyone.

The 23-year-old was on a high last summer after being named player of the tournament as England won the Under-21s European Championship before he signed for Villa on loan with an obligation to buy for £35million.

But things quickly unravelled after when Elliott fell out of favour under new boss Unai Emery and was plunged into the bomb squad given the clause in his deal that the move from Liverpool would become permanent after playing 10 times.

Elliott could not join another club in January as he had already played one league minute for Liverpool before joining on Deadline Day and UEFA rules dictate players can only feature for a maximum of two clubs in one season.

Now the midfielder is back playing with the Reds, his boyhood club, and has spoken publicly for the first time about his lost year.

‘Mentally, it was a very tough one,’ says Elliott, speaking at the Yankee Stadium after featuring in Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham. ‘(Going to Villa) was a learning curve. It was an opportunity for me to experience something new.

‘I don't wish (the situation) upon any other player, because it's not nice at all, but I have no hard feelings. I wish them all the very best. I did really have a lot of love for them. They treated me as one of their own and for that I respect them highly.

Harvey Elliott has revealed the depths of his frustration with his season-long loan to Aston Villa

The academy star fell out of favour with Unai Emery and had little time in his first team

‘But it was tough, mentally and physically. I'm on the other side of it now. I was able to get through it, and achieve something at the end of the season as well (winning a Europa League medal).’

Elliott will be given a chance to impress this pre-season and has played in both wins on this tour of America, where they beat Sunderland in Nashville and Wrexham in New York.

His longer-term future is more uncertain with a second sale highly possible. However, for now, Elliott is keen to take his second chance and win over the trust of new boss Andoni Iraola — who he later described as ‘incredible’ — after former head coach Arne Slot deemed him surplus to requirements.

‘It’s an incredible feeling (to be back),’ he adds. ‘Everyone knows how much I love the club and I've supported them from a very young age, so the feeling never goes of putting a shirt on, representing the club and doing your childhood dream.

‘I wanted a new challenge. I wanted to kind of go and explore something, come out of my comfort zone, I thought personally that would take me on as a player again. Unfortunately, it didn't work out, but the way I see it is, that's last season — now I'm here. It's kind of a second chance, if you want to call it that.

‘Especially with the gaffer coming in. It's another chance to impress and hopefully get in their (good) books. But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best, had a lot of love for them, and they treated me very, very well. Just keep looking forward.

'I'm here now, and I'm trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad.’

‘Since the first day I walked through the door at the AXA (training centre), I had a big beaming smile on my face and, as I've said before about putting the shirt on, I don't want to take these moments for granted.

'Because last season, I thought it was the last opportunity I'd done it. I'm back now. I'm wearing this strip again and putting this shirt on, and I just want to be free, play as much as I can, just enjoy it, because sometimes I don't feel like I do it enough. Playing at Liverpool, there's no better feeling.’

Elliott placed on record that he harboured no ill-feelings to Emery, adding: ‘He explained very, very clearly and a fair few times. The whole club were very apologetic and ultimately, it was a situation that I couldn't control.’

Sports.title: 'Simon Jordan's conspiracy claim is irresponsible and stupid': Kristian Prenga hits out at outspoken presenter and makes bold Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury prediction
Sports.content:
'Simon Jordan's conspiracy claim is irresponsible and stupid': Kristian Prenga hits out at outspoken presenter and makes bold Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury prediction

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Joshua's beaten opponent Kristian Prenga has condemned Simon Jordan after he questioned the legitimacy of their bout.

Joshua stopped Prenga in the second round of their heavyweight fight on Saturday in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia - despite being knocked down twice himself in the first round.

After dropping to the canvas twice in the first round, it looked like the Brit was on course for a shocking defeat until he overcame that major wobble to send Prenga to the floor, making the referee wave off the contest.

Such a dramatic turnaround caused a stir among everyone who watched it - including Simon Jordan who believed there may have been more to the fight than met the eye.

Taking to X, he wrote: 'Not having that … #anthonyjoshua fight... Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how's that ? … Prenga totally different in 2nd.

'Something not quite right , all designed to rinse maximum amount of money...'

Not having that … #anthonyjoshua fight ..:



Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how’s that ? … Prenga totally different in 2nd



Something not quite right , all designed to rinse maximum amount of money … — Simon Jordan (@Sjopinion10) July 25, 2026

Kristian Prenga (left) has hit out at Simon Jordan after his comments over his Anthony Joshua (right) bout

Taking to X, Jordan believed there may have been more to the fight than met the eye after Prenga's sudden decline to lose following a dominant first-round display

Joshua can look forward to a long-anticipated bout with Fury next, one Prenga thinks he'll win

However, Prenga has rubbished those claims and hit out at Jordan for his 'completely false and irresponsible' comments.

Speaking to SveaCasino, the Albanian said: 'What do I make of Simon Jordan's comments? Completely false, and irresponsible for anyone to suggest it. AJ and I have integrity; we would never engage in this stupidity.'

'I felt I needed to preserve energy and catch my breath, so I thought I would start slow and replenish my energy. Unfortunately, it didn't happen, and that slower pace allowed AJ to flip control of the fight to him.'

Joshua is now set to fight long-term rival Tyson Fury in a long-awaited British heavyweight showdown at the back end of this year.

And predicting on who will come out on top between those two, Prenga is adamant that Joshua will give Fury the same ending he faced at the weekend.

'It is tough to predict these things [AJ vs. Fury]. I think both are tough and good fighters but AJ knocks Tyson Fury out,' he continued.

'I would fight Tyson any day. He ran his mouth before my fight with AJ. I would welcome showing him my Albanian power in the ring anytime he is ready for it!'

Sports.title: Fulham bag £8.5m bargain from Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero - and Man City's talks over Ayyoub Bouaddi reach crucial stage: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Fulham bag £8.5m bargain from Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero - and Man City's talks over Ayyoub Bouaddi reach crucial stage: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Hail Cesar as Fulham get their man from Madrid

Fulham have agreed to buy Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid for a bargain £8.5million.

The deal has a similar structure to the one they have agreed for Gonzalo Garcia with Madrid retaining a 30percent sell on clause and matching rights for the 20-year-old.

Fulham are also among the clubs showing interest in Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri and Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Nwaneri also has interest from RB Leipzig and AC Milan.

Cesar Palacios has been secured for a fee of £8.5million

Fredricson moves on

Manchester United defender Tyler Fredricson has agreed a permanent move to Swiss club Lausanne-Sport, subject to registration.

Fredricson made four first-team appearances since he was handed a debut against Wolves in 2025 – when he also won the reserve-team player of the year award – and was on the bench on a number of occasions last season.

United have inserted a substantial sell-on clause and a buy-back clause into the deal.

The 21-year-old, who joined United at Under-9 level, played in every round of United’s successful FA Youth Cup campaign in 2022 until illness ruled him out of the final against Nottingham Forest.

The club confirmed Fredricson’s departure in a statement on Thursday, saying: ‘Everybody at United thanks Tyler for all his efforts during his time with the club and we wish him all the best for the next chapter of his career.’

Fredricson joins United loanee Sekou Kone at the Swiss Super League side.

CHRIS WHEELER

Rashford says no to Roma

Marcus Rashford has no interest in joining Roma this summer as speculation regarding his future grows.

The 28-year-old is set to report to pre-season training with Manchester United in the coming days after returning from his loan spell with Barcelona.

Roma had been one of several clubs linked with a move for the England attacker, but Daily Mail Sport understands a move to the Italian giants does not appeal.

Fulham to spend big on Garcia

Fulham are closing on agreement with Real Madrid over a deal worth £35m for striker Gonzalo Garcia. The deal also includes £2m in bonuses and matching rights.

Madrid have been discussing a buy-back option and a 30 per cent sell-on clause as talks draw to a conclusion.

Fulham also working to add midfielder Cesar Palacios on loan from Madrid.

Gonzalo Garcia looks set to join Fulham from Real Madrid in a deal worth £60m

Hull's Nobel quest

Hull are advancing in talks for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Hull had made enquiries and proposed a £15m offer for the 21-year-old who can play centre back and left back.

Rangers tried to sign Mendy a year ago from Real Betis but Vallecano got him for £2.5m and a 20 per cent sell-on clause.

Hull face competition from Ipswich for Burnley's Florentino Luis but have enquired about Augsburg's midfielder Mert Komur.

Coventry explore Hamer homecoming

Coventry City are exploring a deal to re-sign Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United.

The 29-year-old midfielder has one year left on his deal at Bramall Lane.

The Brazilian made 132 appearances for the club scoring 19 goals which included a strike in the Championship play-off final against Luton Town at Wembley.

Atletico reignite Romero interest

Atletico Madrid have rekindled their interest in Tottenham defender Cristian Romero.

The Argentina international's agents held talks with Inter Milan last weekend and director Piero Ausilio confirmed interest but that the deal would be complicated owing to the financial package.

Atletico Madrid are exploring a potential move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero

Atletico had interest last year and are exploring the figures involved in a deal for the 28-year-old Spurs captain again.

Inter are in the market for centre backs this summer, with one new recruit expected to be John Stones if all goes to plan in his medical today.

Stones set for Inter switch

England defender John Stones has arrived in Italy ahead of his medical with Inter Milan.

Stones, 32, left Manchester City at the end of last season following 10 years with the club.

"Sono entusiasta di essere qui". John Stones è arrivato a Milano ⚫️🔵 pic.twitter.com/Xp2rS66VL9 — Fcinter1908 (@fcin1908it) July 30, 2026

Meanwhile, talks between Manchester City and Lille are reaching a crucial stage over the transfer of Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is ready to make the move now though his club have been keen to keep him in France for another season as part of negotiations.

City are ready to use him this season with Rodri a target for Real Madrid while interest is building in Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders.

City have lost Bernardo Silva and also have interest from Tottenham in Omar Marmoush and Savinho.

Bouaddi was valued around £60m before the World Cup but is now considered to be worth around £80m.

City also want to add another goalkeeper to replace Leeds-bound James Trafford with Marseille's Geronimo Rulli one name under consideration. They also want to strengthen at right-back and on the wing with Chelsea's Pedro Neto and Paris St Germain's Ibrahim Mbaye among names discussed.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Wednesday that the teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now, though the French club would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.
