World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Turkey seeks comprehensive energy cooperation deal with Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement with Iraq following discussions with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Ankara.

Erdogan said that Turkey’s state-owned oil and gas company, TPAO, will operate at Iraq’s Kirkuk oilfield, which is now being developed by British Petroleum (BP), during a joint press conference following a signing ceremony that had been expected to extend the Kirkuk-Ceyhan oil pipeline deal for another year, according to Reuters.

The agreement to renew the decades-old pipeline contract, which regulates shipments along the strategic route, expired on Monday.

After signing three agreements, Erdogan noted that additional deals were anticipated. However, his ministers promptly briefed him on stage, and the two leaders continued with their statements without announcing any further agreements.

The agreement between Iraq and Turkey regarding the crude oil pipeline expired on July 27.

“Our goal is to complete an energy cooperation deal that benefits both parties as quickly as possible,” Erdogan said.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said in a statement on X that TPAO has bought a 15 percent stake in BP Energy Company of Kirkuk Limited (BPECKL), enabling the Turkish business to operate in the sector.

Bayraktar explained the TPAO will cooperate with BPECKL to raise oil production at the Kirkuk field, which has reserves estimated at three million barrels.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to India fall as New Delhi diversifies import sources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil exports to India fell in the first half of 2026, as Indian refineries diversified their crude import sources to minimize the geopolitical risks associated with shipping via the Straits of Hormuz.

According to officials at Indian refining companies and the Indian Ministry of Petroleum, the goal of this measure is to improve supply security.

The drop in Iraqi supplies to India comes at a time when the global oil market is under increased pressure due to security worries along critical maritime routes. This pressure is causing consumers in Asia to split their purchases among many producing countries.

Iraqi oil remains a vital resource for India due to supply security and the high quality of Basra crude.

Indian refiners confirmed they have secured their crude oil requirements until the end of September and have begun arranging purchases for the fourth quarter of the year, despite persistent concerns about the impact of any interruptions to shipping routes on global supply chains.

Meanwhile, Russia remained India’s top crude oil supplier in the first half of the year, while imports from the UAE and Brazil increased.

India’s purchases from Iraq and the United States fell as New Delhi attempted to diversify its supply sources and reduce the risks associated with reliance on a single source.

Indian refiners have warned that increased shipping risks and higher insurance costs, along with declining discounts on Russian oil, are affecting profit margins.

Experts anticipate that continuing instability in the Middle East will raise oil prices and pose new hurdles for Asian oil-importing countries.

World.title: Six Iranian advisors killed in US-Saudi attack on Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A joint US-Saudi attack on targets in Iraq killed six Iranian advisors on Wednesday, according to two Iraqi officials who spoke to the Associated Press (AP).

A meeting that was set for Thursday in Saudi Arabia between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was called off due to recent attacks by armed groups targeting Saudi Arabia.

Al-Zaidi ordered an emergency meeting of Iraq’s National Security Council following the coordinated attacks on the country.

The Iraqi Security Media Cell said in a statement that the meeting was ordered in response to the evolving security situation and the airstrikes that targeted several Iraqi provinces early on Wednesday.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Wednesday that US forces, in cooperation with Saudi armed forces, carried out precision airstrikes targeting sites linked to Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

The coordinated airstrikes were in retaliation for a series of drone attacks targeting US interests and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

CENTCOM said in a statement that the strikes, carried out on July 28, targeted logistics sites and weapons depots allegedly used by Iranian-backed groups. It added that these groups were directed by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to attack US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

US and Saudi fighter jets carried out the strikes, an operation described by CENTCOM as a strong response to more than 30 drone attacks that the IRGC had conducted in the past few days.

Headquarters and sites belonging to the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) in several Iraqi provinces were targeted by the US-Saudi airstrikes in the country.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes test Iraq’s fragile security balance
World.content:
Baghdad – US-Saudi strikes on Iraq killed at least 20 militants, including several Iranians, on Wednesday, according to the Hashed al-Shaabi, an armed Iraqi alliance that includes pro-Iran groups.

The United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed armed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

Washington and Tehran are Iraq’s main allies, but their enmity has long turned the country into a proxy battleground and left successive governments struggling to maintain a delicate balance between the foes.

The Hashed al-Shaabi, also known as the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), said that at least 20 fighters “were martyred and another 32 wounded according to a preliminary toll”.

Two Hashed officials told AFP that five Iranian advisors were among those killed in a strike in the central province of Diyala.

AFP correspondents saw coffins wrapped in Iranian flags during a funeral organised by the Hashed al-Shaabi in Baghdad for those killed.

The Hashed alliance was created in 2014 to fight jihadists before it was formally integrated into the Iraqi armed forces.

It now includes brigades belonging to Iran-backed groups reputed for acting unilaterally.

US President Donald Trump said the strikes were coordinated with the Iraqi government, according to Fox News.

They follow growing US pressure on Baghdad to disarm pro-Iran armed groups, which have frequently targeted US facilities in the country and have long called for the withdrawal of US troops.

Iraq’s new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who came to power this year with Washington’s blessing, vowed to ensure those groups would hand over their weapons, but has faced pushback from some powerful factions.

Earlier this month, Zaidi visited both the United States and Iran.

– ‘Inevitable response’ –

The strikes came after Riyadh said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities, blaming the Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

The most active pro-Iran armed groups are united under an alliance known as the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, which has acted in support of Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks against US bases in Iraq and across the region.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq said “our response to the American enemy is inevitable, and may target its tools in Saudi Arabia”.

But the group added that it would only retaliate after the Arbaeen day of pilgrimage, which falls on Tuesday.

The Arbaeen marks one of the most significant events in the Shia Muslim calendar, during which pilgrims, many from Iran, flock to Iraq to visit the holy shrines.

The pro-Iran groups denied attacking Saudi Arabia and they haven’t claimed any attacks since the US-Iran war resumed earlier this month.

– Violation –

Iraq denounced the US-Saudi strikes and said it rejects “all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented.”

The Ministerial Council for National Security said it would “confront any violation of Iraq’s sovereignty, and prevent any source from using Iraqi territory to threaten neighbouring states”.

It reaffirmed its commitment to ensure the state’s monopoly over weapons.

Zaidi’s government has given those groups that Washington designates as terrorist organisations until September 30 to disarm.

Oil-rich Iraq has been trying to move past decades of war and unrest, but it remains vulnerable to regional and internal flare-ups.

World.title: Iraq condemns US-Saudi strikes, vows tighter control over armed groups
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq condemned U.S.-Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday that targeted Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) sites, calling the attacks a violation of its sovereignty, and announced new measures to tighten state control over security and prevent Iraqi territory from being used to threaten neighboring countries.

Following the attacks, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, which the government said killed and injured many Iraqis.

As regional tensions rose, Al-Zaidi cancelled a planned visit to Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

In a statement published after the meeting, the council said that the strikes happened when Baghdad was already in talks with US and Saudi authorities over suspicions that Iran-aligned armed organizations operating from Iraq committed drone assaults on Saudi land.

“The government was actively engaging with the relevant parties to verify and address the concerns raised by both the Saudi and US sides,” the statement stated, adding that the military action hampered such efforts.

The council authorized a comprehensive security strategy aimed at strengthening state authority across Iraq, combating breaches of Iraqi sovereignty, and prohibiting any party from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten neighboring nations.

The steps reflect Baghdad’s efforts to guarantee that no armed organization may launch assaults from Iraqi soil that could pull the nation into larger regional wars, while also confirming the government’s goal of bringing all security actions under state control.

The council also directed the Foreign Ministry to take legal and diplomatic measures under international law and the United Nations Charter to record the attacks and protect Iraq’s legal rights.

The government condemned the attacks but emphasized that responding to security threats and enforcing the law is solely the responsibility of Iraq’s constitutional institutions.

“The government rejects all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented,” the statement read.

The council underlined Baghdad’s commitment to addressing regional conflicts via diplomacy while maintaining efforts to keep all armaments under state control.

It also restated Iraq’s commitment to carrying out the security agreement guiding the departure of the US-led international coalition by the end of September 2026.

The emergency conference occurred hours after US President Donald Trump claimed that the midnight attacks were coordinated with the Iraqi government, something Baghdad has not officially verified.

Iraqi authorities have openly opposed the operation, emphasizing the political sensitivity of the attacks.

The events highlight Al-Zaidi’s increasingly precarious situation, as he seeks to boost Iraq’s connections with the US and Gulf Arab governments while retaining relations with Iran.

His decision to cancel the Saudi visit underlines the gravity of the problem, as Baghdad seeks to temper regional tensions while preventing Iraqi land from becoming a battlefield for opposing forces.

The government’s current security strategy also suggests a renewed desire to prevent armed groups from operating outside official control, as Baghdad wants to reassure neighboring nations that Iraq will not be used as a springboard for assaults that endanger regional peace.

World.title: Uptime Institute partners with T964 to expand Iraq’s digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Uptime Institute, based in the United States, and Iraqi digital infrastructure company Tech964 Holding Limited (T964) have formed a strategic partnership to help develop Iraq’s digital infrastructure, marking the latest technology agreement to result from Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s investment-focused visit to Washington.

The agreement, signed earlier this month at the U.S.-Iraq Business Summit hosted by the US Chamber of Commerce, names T964 as Uptime Institute’s business partner in Iraq to promote international data center standards, professional training, and the development of resilient digital infrastructure.

The agreement is part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy beyond oil by increasing digital infrastructure, attracting technological investment, and bolstering industries including cloud computing, artificial intelligence, financial technology, and cybersecurity.

T964, one of Iraq’s major private digital infrastructure businesses, has announced that it would collaborate with the Uptime Institute to implement internationally recognized standards for the country’s expanding network of data centers, as well as increase technical competence and operational best practices.

The partnership is anticipated to help establish carrier-neutral data centers, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud services, and AI-ready digital platforms, all of which the government believes are important to modernizing public services and stimulating private-sector investment.

The pact follows a series of technological ties announced during Al-Zaidi’s tour to the United States, during which Iraq inked more than 50 agreements totaling more than $60 billion in the energy, banking, infrastructure, industrial, and technology sectors.

Improving digital infrastructure has become a key component of Iraq’s long-term economic plan, as the country strives to lessen reliance on oil earnings and establish a knowledge-based economy capable of attracting foreign technology businesses while also encouraging homegrown innovation.

The alliance also underscores increased US private-sector interest in Iraq’s digital economy, especially as demand for secure data centers, cloud computing capacity, and AI infrastructure in the Middle East grows.

Iraq has increasingly prioritized digital infrastructure for foreign investment alongside energy and transportation, with officials claiming that internationally certified data centers and modern telecommunications networks will be critical to supporting e-government services, digital banking, e-commerce, and artificial intelligence, as well as strengthening Iraq’s role as an emerging regional technology hub.

World.title: OpenAI says rogue AI agent attack hit other companies
World.content:
San Francisco – ChatGPT maker OpenAI has revealed that an autonomous artificial intelligence agent which hacked a popular platform for computer programmers also attempted to breach four other companies during the incident.

In an update late Tuesday to a blog post detailing its probe into the incident, OpenAI said its AI agent affected these “publicly-available services,” though it did not name the companies.

The revelation broadens a cyber incident that OpenAI described as unprecedented and which began when two of its models hacked Hugging Face, a site developers use to store and share AI models and code.

OpenAI admitted last week that during testing, the models powering the agent broke out of their confined environment and connected to the internet to find ways to infiltrate Hugging Face.

AI agents — systems that act autonomously to complete tasks rather than just responding to step-by-step prompts in a chatbot — are hailed across the industry as the next chapter in AI.

But they raise the specter among the public of rogue computers acting on their own.

In its update of the events leading to the hack, OpenAI said it found a handful of instances where the AI models came across login details that other companies had left exposed online, and used them to get into accounts on outside services.

In the Hugging Face episode, the models broke into four accounts across four different services, OpenAI said. One served as a “staging path” — a kind of pit stop to route the agent’s activity and cover its tracks — and another as a place to store data.

The remaining two were only accessed in a “read-only manner” and were not used to help break into Hugging Face, OpenAI said.

The company said it was contacting the owners of the affected accounts and had “not seen evidence of broader impact to these providers or other accounts on their services.”

– Better sandbox –

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview published Tuesday that the company had “paused” its own testing after the incident while it improved the security around its “sandboxing” — the process of isolating safety testing in a controlled environment.

The incident also triggered a petition signed by over 1,000 employees at cutting-edge AI companies, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, calling on the US government to help slow the release of the most advanced AI models.

This in turn has sparked accusations from other Silicon Valley players close to the White House that the companies are inviting tighter government regulation on AI in order to protect their business models and block the emergence of rivals.

The incident has also drawn rumblings from some observers that OpenAI is taking advantage of it to market the power of its state-of-the-art models.

The same accusation was leveled at Anthropic when it held back the public release of its powerful Mythos model over cybersecurity concerns.

Anthropic released a stripped-down version of Mythos, called Fable 5, but the US government quickly forced it to take it down, citing national security risks.

It gave the green light in late June after some modifications were made.

World.title: Why Bankipur bypoll grabbed national attention and what it means for Prashant Kishor
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Will Bihar's Bankipur stand with the

, as it has over the years, or will it give

a victory on debut? Or, will Tejashwi Yadav's RJD will finally have something to cheer about? The fate of the three key contenders in the crucial byelection have been sealed in EVM machines and the people's verdict will be known on August 3, when the votes are counted.

So, what made this by-election grab so much of national attention?

The Bankipur bypoll was necessitated after

, who represented the urban Patna seat for nearly two decades, resigned from Bihar assembly to become a member of Rajya Sabha. This followed his elevation as BJP president earlier this year. The Bankipur seat has been a BJP bastion for over three decades with Nitin Nabin's family winning from the constituency for over 35 years.

Before Nitin Nabin, the constituency was represented by his father Nabin Kishore Prasad Sinha.

And that explains why winning today's election is so important for the BJP.

But what could have been a cakewalk for BJP and its chief Nitin Nabin was turned into a formidable challenge with the entry of election strategist turned politician Prashant Kishor in the election arena. Kishor's entry made today's election a three-cornered contest.





For Prashant Kishor, whose party Jan Suraj was outrightly rejected by the people of the state in the assembly elections last year, this bypoll is a litmus test.

Kishor, who has scripted success stories of several parties and leaders as an election-strategist, would hope that the people of Bankipur would give his political career a much-needed boost.

And finally the RJD, the third pole of this electoral battle, would desperately hope that the people of Bankipur would have voted today for a change.

The RJD, which was literally decimated by the ruling NDA in the 2025 assembly elections, will be keen to prove a political point.

Polling concluded with a voter turnout of 34.16 per cent among the nearly 3.8 lakh eligible electors, with counting of votes scheduled for August 3.

As expected, the polling today was marked by allegations and counter allegations. Both Prashant Kishor and RJD candidate Rekha Gupta trained their guns at the BJP.

Prashant Kishore alleged that more than 30 of his party workers had been arrested during polling and accused the police administration of acting "completely one-sidedly" to intimidate voters and help the BJP. "In an organised manner, wherever people of Jan Suraaj have set up tables, these people are taking them away.

Across entire Bankipur, it's evident that it's not the BJP contesting this bypoll but the police force.

People are being intimidated right from the night by going to their homes; some are being arrested," he said.

RJD candidate Rekha Gupta accused BJP workers of violating the Model Code of Conduct by allegedly attempting to influence voters at polling stations. âThe BJP has hatched a conspiracy. All the polling agents have been given BJP ID cards,â Gupta alleged, while urging the election authorities to take note of the matter," she said.

The BJP rubbished these charges and instead accused that Jan Suraaj Party workers were "attempting to cast fraudulent votes" in the Bankipur assembly bypoll and urged the Election Commission to strengthen verification of electors. BJP state general secretary Nitin Abhishek wrote a letter to the returning officer of the assembly, claiming that such practices undermine the fundamental principles of democracy.

"It has come to our notice that representatives and workers associated with the Jan Suraaj Party are attempting to compromise the integrity of the polling process by attempting to cast fraudulent/fake votes in the Bankipur bypoll," the BJP said in the letter.

Why Bankipur is being watched closely

Bypolls, anywhere in the country, attract little interest. For the NDA, which won 202 out of 243 seats in the assembly elections, the result of one seat should hardly matter.

However, this bypoll is the first election after Samrat Choudhary took over the chief ministerial post from Nitish Kumar.

The assembly election was fought with the NDA projecting Nitish as its chief ministerial face. However, Nitish resigned from the top post to take up a Rajya Sabha seat, handing over the reins to Choudhary.

The Bankipur bypoll offers the first electoral test of public approval for Choudhary as chief minister.

Realising the importance of the seat, the BJP left little to chance in Bankipur. The party mobilised an entire roster of NDA ministers, former ministers, MPs and MLAs to campaign for its candidate, Neeraj Kumar Sinha.

Former chief minister Nitish Kumar also joined the campaign through a video appeal, urging voters to support the BJP candidate. On the ground, the party kept up a hectic schedule of bike rallies, Adhivakta Samwad, Chikitsa Samwad, roadshows and door-to-door outreach in an effort to consolidate support.

Bankipurâs caste composition also makes the bypoll an interesting contest. The constituency has nearly 3.8 lakh voters, with Kayasths and Yadavs together making up around 25 per cent of the electorate.

The BJP has traditionally enjoyed strong support among Kayasths. Muslims and Chandravanshis together account for nearly 20 per cent of voters, while Vaishyas, Dalits, Bhumihars, Rajputs, Brahmins, Kurmis and Kushwahas each constitute between 3 per cent and 8 per cent of the electorate.

Tough road for BJP?

Prashant Kishorâs political gambit, along with developments such as Bharat Tiwariâs encounter and the recent student protests in Patna, has made the bypoll harder for the BJP than the party initially anticipated.

The first setback came even before the campaign gathered pace. The BJPâs initial candidate, Abhishek Kumar Sinha, withdrew from the contest after reports emerged that a close family member had been convicted in the fodder scam.

The BJP later replaced him with 32-year-old Neeraj Kumar Sinha after the partyâs Central Election Committee approved his candidature.

Another challenge for the ruling party is the reported resentment among sections of the upper-caste community following the June encounter of Bharat Tiwari.

Tiwari was killed during a standoff with the police and Special Task Force personnel on June 17. In the aftermath, chief minister Samrat Choudhary met Tiwariâs family and assured them of a transparent investigation, the preservation of evidence and strict action against those found guilty.

The recent student unrest has added another dimension to the campaign. Bankipur is home to several colleges, universities and coaching institutes, making students a significant voting bloc in the constituency.

Large student protests over issues such as employment, education and alleged irregularities in competitive examinations have heightened political engagement among young voters.

Police action during some of these demonstrations also attracted widespread attention on social media, ensuring that education, jobs and governance remain central themes in the bypoll campaign.

Both Kishor and RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav blamed Samrat Choudhary for the action against protesters.

The state government, too, was quick to respond. After a Bihar bandh called by Left-wing student unions on July 25, police detained close to 700 protesters, of whom nearly half were let off after they turned out to be minors.

While talking to The Times of India, political analyst Kumar Vijay predicted a tough contest on July 30.

"BJP initially thought this election would be fairly easy. Perhaps thatâs why it made a mistake in choosing its candidate. And when the second candidate was chosen, he too appeared to be a potentially weak opponent to Prashant Kishor, despite the constituency having several prominent leaders to choose from," Vijay said.

"But now BJP is seeing this contest turn tight. Thatâs why it has fielded 50 star campaigners for a single bypoll.

And wherever these leaders have gone to campaign, they have faced opposition. This did not happen earlier," he told TOI.

He added that if Prashant Kishor manages to consolidate Muslim, Yadav, women and fringe voters, it could spell trouble for the BJP.

"It is time for the BJP to reconsider its strategy, way of working and decision-making process," he added.

Meanwhile, BJP state vice-president Santosh Pathak asserted that the party would easily win the bypoll.

Although he acknowledged resentment among upper-caste voters, he claimed that they would ultimately vote for the BJP on July 30.

"Prashant Kishorâs entry has only added glamour to the election. Beyond that, there is nothing new about this contest. This time too, we will win by a good margin," Pathak said while talking to The Times of India.

"There is some resentment among Brahmins and Bhumihars, but they will still vote for the BJP.

Bankipur is a backward-oriented seat. The people creating all the buzz are not voters of this assembly constituency," he added.

Why itâs an all-at-stake contest for PK

Describing the contest as a âreferendumâ on the two-month-old BJP-led NDA government in Bihar, Prashant sought to transform what would ordinarily have been a local bypoll into one of the stateâs most closely watched electoral battles.

"The upcoming by-election is going to be a referendum on the working of the two-month-old government of Samrat Choudhary," Prashant had said after announcing his candidature.

"If the BJP wins, I will have no hesitation in conceding that the saffron party continues to enjoy public support. If we win, it shall be for them to read the writing on the wall," he added.

Despite several prominent leaders leaving Jan Suraaj, Kishor remained visible through mohalla meetings, adda baithaks, chai baithaks, padyatras, interactions with intellectuals and Jan Samwad programmes.

However, the bypoll is also a test of Kishorâs own political project.

A victory would give Jan Suraaj its first electoral breakthrough and help the party carve out political space in Bihar.

A defeat, however, would make the road to revival even harder for the party. With no major election scheduled in Bihar before the 2029 Lok Sabha polls, the stakes could hardly be higher.

Challenge for RJD

This bypoll carries almost as much weight for the RJD, which put in a lacklustre show in the assembly elections and is now keen to keep its Muslim-Yadav vote bank from eroding.

At the same time, Prashant Kishorâs rising profile, even if symbolic for now and confined to a single seat, poses a different kind of threat: the RJD cannot afford to cede its place as the principal challenger to the BJP.

That dilemma captures the existential challenge confronting Tejashwi Yadavâs party. Should Jan Suraaj emerge as the leading anti-BJP force in Bankipur, it would inevitably chip away at the RJDâs standing as Biharâs primary opposition party.

The RJD has fielded Rekha Gupta, also known as

Rekha Kumari

, for the bypoll. She had contested the same seat in the November 2025 assembly polls, where she secured close to 47,000 votes.

What the opinion poll says

An opinion poll by VoteVibe suggests that the BJP retains the upper hand in Bankipur, but Prashant Kishorâs entry has transformed what was once seen as a one-sided contest.

The survey projects the BJP to secure 44.9 per cent of the vote, comfortably ahead of Jan Suraaj at 33.8 per cent, while the RJD is estimated to finish a distant third with 17.8 per cent.

The RJD appears to have suffered the biggest setback. According to the poll, its vote share is projected to decline from 29.8 per cent in the 2025 assembly polls to 17.8 per cent in Bankipur.

The Bankipur bypoll has all the makings of a David and Goliath contest, though it is not entirely clear who fits which role. The BJP appears to be the giant. It has held the seat continuously since 1995, is backed by the resources of the ruling government and has deployed 50 star campaigners for a single bypoll.

Yet the party enters the contest on the defensive after replacing its initial candidate and grappling with discontent among sections of its traditional upper-caste support base.

PK, by contrast, looks like David, a challenger with no seats to his name and a party still finding its feet after last year's washout. But he carries the slingshot of celebrity, momentum from Biharâs student protests and a campaign built entirely around unseating the giant.

World.title: 'How is unelected minister continuing for over six months?' SC raps Bihar govt
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Thursday questioned the Bihar government over the continuation of Panchayati Raj minister Deepak Prakash, asking the state to explain how he remained in office beyond the six-month constitutional limit without being elected to the state legislature.

The matter was mentioned before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, which observed that the issue involved a pure question of law under Article 164(4) of the Constitution.

Mentioning the plea, the petitioner's counsel said, "My Lord, it is now over six months and he continues as a minister."

Counsel appearing for the Bihar government informed the court that the matter was already listed for hearing on August 27.

"The matter is already listed on August 27. I leave it to Your Lordships," the state's counsel said.

Responding to the submissions, CJI Surya Kant remarked, "This is a pure question of law. The State will have to explain how a minister is continuing for over six months without being elected. You have to explain it."

The petition challenges Deepak Prakash's continuation as a minister under Article 164(4) of the Constitution, which permits a person who is not a member of the state legislature to be appointed as a minister for a maximum of six consecutive months.





The provision requires the minister to get elected to either House of the state legislature within that period, failing which the individual must cease to hold office.

Filed by social activist Rakesh Kumar Singh, the plea contends that Prakash was first inducted into the Bihar cabinet on November 20, 2025, despite not being a member of either the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council. After the Nitish Kumar government fell on April 15, 2026, Prakash was reappointed in the new government headed by chief minister Samrat Choudhary on May 7, 2026.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The petitioner argues that the six-month exemption under Article 164(4) is a one-time constitutional concession that cannot be reset through reappointment, a cabinet reshuffle or a change in government during the tenure of the same Legislative Assembly.

The plea relies on the Supreme Court's 2001 judgment in S.R. Chaudhari v. State of Punjab, which held that Article 164(4) cannot be used to repeatedly appoint a non-legislator as minister without securing election to the legislature, emphasising that the provision is an exception that must be interpreted narrowly to preserve democratic accountability.

World.title: From LPG to Rabi fertilisers: PM Modi reviews Middle East crisis preparedness
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday chaired a high-level meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) to review the ongoing conflict in Middle East and assess India's preparedness to deal with its impact.

The meeting reviewed the geopolitical situation, the availability of fuel and fertilisers, the safety of Indian citizens and the diaspora and measures to protect Indian seafarers operating in conflict zones. This was the fourth special CCS meeting held on the issue.

During the meet, several top cabinet ministers including Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh and NSA chief Ajit Doval were also present.

The Cabinet Secretary briefed the committee on the steps taken to ensure uninterrupted supplies of petroleum products, including crude oil, LPG and LNG.

According to the briefing, India has diversified its LPG procurement sources and that the stock position of major petroleum products remains adequate.

The government said sufficient crude oil supplies have enabled public sector refineries to operate at utilisation levels of over 100%, ensuring continued production of petrol, diesel and other fuels. It also highlighted ongoing efforts to expand piped natural gas (PNG) connections, strengthen the National Gas Grid, increase LNG import and regasification capacity and improve city gas distribution networks.





The CCS also reviewed fertiliser availability ahead of the upcoming Rabi season. PM Modi further directed officials to take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted fertiliser supplies and explore alternate sources wherever required.

The situation of Indian seafarers serving on domestic and foreign-flagged vessels in conflict zones also came up for discussion. PM directed the government to establish a dedicated mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families.

Emphasising the need to protect Indian nationals overseas, PM Modi said every effort should be made to safeguard both Indian citizens and the Indian diaspora from the impact of the conflict, according to Press Information Bureau.

PM Modi also stressed the importance of reducing dependence on conventional energy sources and called for greater emphasis on renewable energy, including solar power and other non-fossil fuel-based sources, to strengthen India's long-term energy security.

Calling for a whole-of-government approach, PM Modi directed ministries and departments to continue working in close coordination. He also asked officials to establish a unified monitoring mechanism to regularly track developments in Middle East and ensure quick implementation of measures required to protect the interests of Indian citizens.

The ongoing conflict in Middle East involving the United States, Iran and Israel has affected global energy markets and supply chains. India has also faced concerns over LPG supplies and energy security due to disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, leading the government to regularly review the evolving situation and preparedness measures.

World.title: NEET-UG 2026 case: CBI links leak to teachers who set paper, did translation work - report
World.content:
Protest against NEET UG paper leak was held at Jantar Mantar (ANI images)

CBI may recommend changes

NEW DELHI: NEET-UG 2026 was compromised after the same set of individuals was entrusted with both question-setting and translation, exposing a key procedural lapse.The teachers entrusted with setting and translating the NEET-UG 2026 question paper allegedly memorised the final questions, reconstructed them from memory and shared them with a select group of students attending their private coaching classes, PTI cited as sources revealed.The paper setters â chemistry teacher P V Kulkarni, physics teacher Manisha Gurunath Mandhare and biology teacher Manisha Sanjay Havaldar â were responsible for both preparing the question paper and translating it into Marathi, giving them prolonged access to the final version ahead of the May 3 examination.Although the experts were kept in a sanitised environment during the paper preparation process, they were allowed to return home each day, the statement reads. During this period, they allegedly reconstructed the questions from memory and shared them with a select group of students, marking them as "very important" without revealing they were from the upcoming NEET examination.Investigators said the questions later spread beyond the coaching classes after local beautician Manisha Waghmare allegedly obtained the reconstructed question bank from some students. She allegedly typed the questions into a paper-like format and sold them to Dhananjay Nivrutti Lokhande, who circulated them through a network of middlemen across multiple states in exchange for lakhs of rupees.The agency has informally conveyed the issue to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and is likely to recommend separating the two responsibilities in its formal recommendations.The incident came into light after one aspirant received the purported question paper and alerted the NTA, which cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 examination on May 12.The Union education ministry subsequently handed the probe to the CBI, which arrested 13 people, including the three subject experts, Waghmare, coaching institute associates and alleged middlemen.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Lok Sabha passes Vande Mataram Bill, Iran says destroyed 3 US F-35 jets & more
World.content:
Lok Sabha passes Vande Mataram Bill amid opposition protests over NEET paper leak and alleged police action on students.

passes amid opposition protests over and alleged police action on students. Over 200 academicians write to Priyanka Gandhi, objecting to her remarks on IIT Madras director V Kamakoti.

Nitin Gadkari says E20 fuel may reduce mileage by up to 6%, but tests found no engine failures linked to ethanol blending

Hockey India explains saffron World Cup jersey, citing better visibility on blue turf and national symbolism

Iran claims it destroyed three US F-35 fighter jets in Jordan; Washington has not confirmed the claim.

Here are top five news stories:

Lok Sabha passes Vande Mataram Bill as opposition protests

Parliament remained disrupted as the Lok Sabha passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, extending legal protection to Vande Mataram.

The opposition protested over the alleged police action against student protesters and demanded home minister Amit Shah's resignation.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticised the government's handling of the NEET paper leak and called for broader education reforms.

'Mockery is no substitute for reasoned engagement': Oer 200 academicians write to Priyanka Gandhi

More than 200 academicians have written an open letter to Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra objecting to her remarks, widely seen as targeting IIT Madras director Prof V Kamakoti during the Lok Sabha debate on the anti-paper leak Bill.

The signatories said Parliament should encourage reasoned debate rather than ridicule and argued that reducing a scholar to a label undermines scientific temper.

They highlighted Kamakoti's academic achievements and contributions to research, urging public representatives to challenge ideas with evidence instead of personal remarks that discourage academic participation in public discourse.

E20 petrol may cut mileage by up to 6%, but no engine failures found: Gadkari

Union minister Nitin Gadkari informed Parliament that petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20) can reduce vehicle fuel efficiency by 2% to 6%, depending on the vehicle and its age.





However, extensive testing by ARAI, SIAM and Indian Oil found no evidence of engine failures linked to E20 fuel.

Gadkari said the fuel improves acceleration, ride quality and reduces carbon emissions by around 30%. He added that India's ethanol blending programme has been implemented gradually with scientific validation and manufacturers continue to honour warranty claims for E20-compatible vehicles.

India's hockey teams will wear saffron instead of blue at the 2026 World Cup

Hockey India has defended its decision to replace the traditional blue jersey with saffron for the men's and women's teams at the 2026 FIH Hockey World Cup.

The federation said the move was driven by technical concerns, as blue jerseys blended with modern blue synthetic pitches, affecting player visibility.

Coaches and players suggested alternative colours before saffron was selected. Hockey India also said saffron symbolises courage and national pride as one of the colours of the Indian flag. Former captain Viren Rasquinha criticised the decision, saying blue remains part of India's hockey identity.

World.title: Quote of the day by Bhagat Singh: ‘Study so that you are able to meet the arguments of your opponents,’ and why knowledge is the strongest answer to disagreement
World.content:
Quote of the day by Bhagat Singh

âStudy so that you are able to meet the arguments of your opponents.â â

Bhagat Singh

Reading broadens the argument before it strengthens it

Knowledge changes the quality of disagreement

Why the quote still matters

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Every disagreement presents a choice. One person raises their voice, while another repeats familiar slogans. A third begins asking questions, searching for evidence and trying to understand where the other side is coming from before responding. Bhagat Singh's advice belongs firmly in the third tradition. He treats study as preparation for conversation rather than examination, and knowledge as something that sharpens judgement instead of feeding pride. His words suggest that the strength of an argument depends less on confidence than on how carefully it has been built.Bhagat Singh wrote constantly throughout his short life. While imprisoned, he read history, economics, political philosophy, literature and revolutionary thought with remarkable discipline, filling notebooks with quotations and reflections from writers across the world. His reading shaped his politics, though it also shaped the way he argued. He believed conviction carried greater weight when it rested on careful thought instead of emotion alone. That is why this line continues to resonate. It speaks to anyone who hopes to persuade rather than simply win.People usually begin with opinions. Study asks them to examine where those opinions come from. A reader who spends time with different authors soon discovers that intelligent people have disagreed about almost every important question in history.Freedom, justice, religion, economics and education have all been debated across generations, often by thinkers who arrived at very different conclusions while drawing on equally serious scholarship.That process does something valuable. It slows certainty. Someone who has read widely becomes more careful with conclusions because they understand how many perspectives exist beyond their own experience. A lawyer prepares by studying both sides of a case. A scientist examines competing explanations before accepting one. A historian compares sources instead of relying on a single account. Strong arguments grow from that habit of testing ideas before defending them.Bhagat Singh encouraged the same discipline. He wanted young people to read because reading develops the habit of thinking independently. A belief borrowed from someone else can be repeated. A belief reached through study can be explained, defended and refined.Modern life makes it easy to respond immediately. Social media rewards quick reactions, television debates often value interruption over discussion and public conversations frequently become contests of personality rather than ideas. In that environment, Bhagat Singh's advice feels remarkably current.Knowledge does not eliminate disagreement. It changes the way disagreement is handled. A person who understands the history behind an issue is less likely to reduce it to slogans. Someone familiar with evidence can separate facts from assumptions. Even when no agreement is reached, the conversation becomes more useful because each side has something substantial to contribute.Many of history's greatest debates produced progress because participants challenged one another with ideas rather than insults. Scientific discoveries emerged through criticism. Constitutional democracies developed through public debate. Universities exist because questioning accepted wisdom has always been considered an essential part of learning. Those traditions survive only when people value understanding as much as persuasion.Education is often treated as a path towards employment, and it certainly serves that purpose. Bhagat Singh points to another purpose that receives far less attention. Reading equips people to think clearly when confronted with difficult questions. It teaches them to recognise weak reasoning, appreciate strong evidence and remain open to learning even while defending deeply held beliefs.That lesson extends far beyond politics. Families resolve differences through conversation. Workplaces depend on people exchanging ideas without resentment. Democracies function because citizens weigh competing arguments before making choices. In each of those settings, knowledge becomes more than personal achievement.It becomes a public responsibility.Bhagat Singh's words endure because they place faith in the power of ideas. They remind readers that disagreement has never been settled by volume alone. Lasting influence belongs to those who understand an issue well enough to answer it with reason, evidence and the patience to keep learning.

World.title: Govt summons Meta executives again over temporary restriction of PM Modi's Facebook post
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has summoned senior executives of US technology giant Meta after Facebook briefly restricted Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video message last week, with the government seeking an explanation from the company over the incident.

The video, first uploaded by PM Modi on Instagram and later shared on Facebook, was temporarily unavailable on the social media platform before being restored. Meta had earlier said the restriction was caused by an inadvertent error.

"We have asked Meta to come in at the highest level and explain what is happening," S Krishnan, secretary in the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), said on Thursday.

Krishnan did not specify which Meta executives had been asked to appear before the ministry.

According to the MeitY secretary, Meta has informed the government that it has introduced new protocols for accounts belonging to prominent public figures to prevent similar incidents from recurring.

Meta India did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment on Thursday.

The video, posted by Modi on July 23, marked his first public address on the nationwide student protests over the alleged NEET paper leak, which eventually culminated in the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.





The post has since garnered more than 404 million views on Instagram.

The latest summons comes days after Meta acknowledged that the post had been removed by mistake.

"The content was removed in error and has since been restored," a Meta spokesperson had said after the incident.

World.title: No action against CJP protesters: Delhi government
World.content:
The Home Department of the Delhi government on Thursday (July 30, 2026) issued an order that no adverse legal action will be taken against people involved in the protests against the NEET-UG paper leak issue.

“The protection, however, shall not extend to persons having criminal antecedents, as mandated in the order of Hon’ble Supreme Court mentioned above,” it said, citing a verdict dated July 28.

Also read | Centre’s assurance cannot override statutory processes governing withdrawal of FIRs, experts say

If anyone has been arrested or detained in cases related to the protests, the process for reviewing the arrests and releasing the arrested persons will be undertaken “expeditiously”, as per the order.

“Government of NCT of Delhi does not propose to take any further adverse action against the individuals involved in the protests, and the matter shall be treated as closed without any future proceedings on this account,” the order said.

However, Delhi Home Minister Ashish Sood clarified in a statement that this relief will not apply to individuals who already have criminal cases registered against them or those who indulged in violence, vandalism, or any other unlawful activities under the guise of the protest.

“Such persons will face action strictly in accordance with the law. The government fully respects the democratic right to peaceful expression, but no leniency will be shown towards those who disrupt law and order or engage in violent activities,” Mr. Sood said.

The CJP had said that the government’s agreement was to withdraw cases against “all protesters” and not take any action against them in the future in relation to the protests.

On Saturday (July 25, 2026), the CJP called off its 36-day protest after the Central government agreed to its three main demands, including the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Education Minister. The other two demands were withdrawal of cases against all protesters and no future action against them, as well as compensation to families whose children died by suicide due to the NEET paper leak.

On Monday (July 27, 2026) the CJP warned of fresh protests, accusing the Centre of violating its assurance that no punitive action would be taken against protesters. Later in the evening, the CJP said that West Bengal, Assam and Bihar had announced to withdraw FIRs.

World.title: Police find no homicide angle in Nilambur newborn’s death
World.content:
The police have found no signs of homicide in the death of a newborn baby whose body was found in a waste bucket in the washroom of a private hospital at Akampadam near Nilambur on Tuesday (July 28, 2026).

The preliminary post-mortem examination conducted at Government Medical College Hospital, Manjeri, indicated that the death was not caused by a criminal act. The police said the exact cause of death would be known only after receiving the pathology report from a laboratory in Kozhikode.

Doctors have suggested that the death may have occurred due to breathing difficulties during delivery or injuries sustained when the baby fell during birth.

The newborn’s body was found in a waste disposal bucket in a toilet at a private hospital at Akampadam on Tuesday morning. A 28-year-old woman from Chaliyar, who is currently undergoing treatment at the Government District Hospital at Nilambur under police observation, is being investigated in connection with the incident.

The police said the woman had reached the hospital around Monday (July 27, 2026) midnight with her husband and relatives following bleeding. She had not informed the hospital staff about her pregnancy.

As the hospital did not have a gynaecologist, she was advised to seek treatment elsewhere. She later entered the toilet with the pretext of changing clothes, where she delivered the baby. A sanitation worker found the newborn’s body the next morning.

World.title: Coimbatore District Police hold meeting with private, omni bus operators
World.content:
Coimbatore District Superintendent of Police A. Pavan Kumar Reddy on Thursday held a meeting with private and omni bus operators to discuss road safety, traffic management, public awareness and measures to prevent traffic violations. Over 100 persons, including Deputy Superintendents of Police, Inspectors, Transport Department officers, private bus owners, office-bearers and members of private bus associations and representatives of omni bus associations from across the district, attended the meeting.

The SP stressed that reducing road accidents involving private buses and ensuring the safety of the public is a shared responsibility. He emphasised that special care must be taken while women, children, senior citizens, and persons with disabilities are board and alight from buses.

Transport Department officials explained the harmful effects of using high-decibel pressure horns, unnecessary decorative lighting and excessively bright headlights.

The SP informed bus operators that a period of 15 days would be granted for compliance with the instructions and traffic regulations discussed during the meeting. Joint enforcement drives would be conducted throughout the district by the police and the Transport Department after two weeks.

World.title: Bhogapuram airport commute: ₹300 by RTC e-bus, ₹800 to ₹1,500 by cab from Visakhapatnam
World.content:
A seat on the electric bus to Visakhapatnam’s new airport at Bhogapuram is expected to cost around ₹300. The same journey by cab is likely to cost between ₹700 and ₹1,500.

The fare structure is taking shape ahead of the inauguration of the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram, on Saturday (August 1, 2026). Commercial flight operations are scheduled to begin on August 17.

The pricing largely reflects the distance involved. The airport is located off National Highway-16, near the Vizianagaram district border, around 43 to 50 km from the Visakhapatnam city.

When The Hindu drove from its office in Seethammadhara to the new airport site recently, the journey took about 75 minutes. From CMR Central in Gajuwaka, the distance is 60.4 km, making it a longer trip when compared to the other big cities airports serving Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Navi Mumbai, which sit far outside. From Anandapuram, it is 23 km and about half an hour’s journey.

Sources in the corporation said: “The Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) expects to price its airport electric buses fare at about ₹300 from the core city (Visakhapatnam) and about ₹100 from the Madhurawada belt, 34 km away.” The fare card is yet to be approved and is expected before commercial operations begin, they added.

In the first phase, the corporation will run 20 electric buses, with 10 e-buses on each of the two routes.

The first route will run from Gajuwaka through NAD Junction, Gurudwara, Maddilapalem, Madhurawada and Anandapuram to the airport. The travel time is about one hour and 45 minutes, about 12 minutes longer than a cab journey.

The second route runs from Gajuwaka through Scindia, Visakhapatnam Railway Station, the VMRDA Park on Beach Road, IT Hills in Madhurawada, Marikavalasa and Anandapuram. The journey is expected to take about two hours. Officials said services would be stepped up and routes added, depending on demand, after the airport opens.

The cab market

At about 4.30 p.m. on Thursday (July 30, 2026), when The Hindu checked app-based rides—Ola, Uber and Rapido— the fares quoted from ₹1,000 to ₹1,100 from the city’s arterial roads, ₹700 to ₹900 from Madhurawada, and up to ₹1,500 from Gajuwaka, depending on traffic, demand and the operator. The cheapest ride checked was ₹700 from the Madhurawada belt; and the highest was ₹1,440 from CMR Central. No app-based fare is fixed. According to the aggregator rate guides rush-hours lift fares 1.4 to 1.6 times, while rain and weekends can push prices to nearly twice the normal fare. World.title: Ten years and 7 PMs later, did Brexit make a difference?
World.content:
When Andy Burnham took charge as the U.K.’s Prime Minister on July 20, he became the seventh occupant of 10 Downing Street since the country decided to exit the European Union (EU) by a narrow margin in the Brexit referendum held in June 2016.

The fact that the U.K. has never seen these many Prime Ministers in any 10-year period in at least the last five decades speaks to the political volatility the country is witnessing. Although one cannot attribute the unprecedented revolving door of Prime Ministers to Brexit alone, the instability provides the backdrop to test whether the U.K.’s exit from the EU — which legally came into force in January 2020 — made any difference in meeting the objectives it purportedly wanted to achieve.

The two key arguments made in favour of the exit were to control migration and enable the U.K. to chart its own path in trade by freeing the country from the “unfair” regulations imposed by the EU.

Taking back control of borders

The ‘Vote Leave’ campaign used the famous slogan “take back control”, meaning in part to increase control over the U.K.’s borders and break free from the EU’s free movement programme, which allows citizens of member countries to live and travel across other member countries without a visa.

Seven months after the referendum, the then Prime Minister Theresa May said, “Brexit must mean control of the number of people who come to Britain from Europe.” The Conservative Party manifesto for the 2019 election, which Boris Johnson won to become the Prime Minister, promised that there would be fewer lower-skilled immigrants and that overall immigration would come down. Instead, the data show that net migration (immigration minus emigration) moved in the opposite direction, although immigration from EU countries fell.

After free movement between the U.K. and the EU ended in January 2021, net migration reached 8,91,000 in 2022 and 8,48,000 in 2023, more than three times the 2016 level. In fact, the total net migration of 2.7 million in the five-year period from 2021 to 2025 was more than double the 1.27 million recorded in the five years before the Brexit vote (2012-2016).

Brexit campaigners had promised to cut overall numbers by replacing EU free movement with a common system covering migrants from everywhere. While a unified system was put in place, the trends for EU and non-EU migrants diverged sharply.

In the 2012-2016 period, net migration from EU countries to the U.K. marginally exceeded the country’s overall net migration figure. For instance, in 2016, net migration from EU and non-EU countries stood at 2,53,000 and 90,000 respectively, while 94,000 U.K. nationals left the country. This left the U.K.’s net migration in 2016 at 2,49,000. The trend has since reversed: from mid-2022, net migration from the EU to the U.K. has been negative. Thus, Brexit did not reduce migration but altered the composition of migrants.

Mixed outcomes in trade

Trade tells another complicated story. Brexit campaigners touted leaving the EU as a chance to reduce dependence on the bloc’s regulations and expand commerce with the rest of the world while continuing to have full access to the European market. The COVID-19 pandemic coincided with the U.K.’s formal exit from the EU and the U.K.-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement. The agreement was a last-ditch free trade deal to continue zero tariffs and avoid reverting to the World Trade Organization’s rules, which Ms. May claimed would allow “for the freest possible trade in goods and services between Britain and the EU’s member states.”

Though the U.K.’s exports to countries in the EU, in current prices, have grown year-on-year since 2021, its trade deficit has also widened due to higher imports from these countries.

Across each year from 2012 to 2025, the U.K. ran a trade deficit with EU countries and a surplus with non-EU countries. Though the pattern held, the U.K.’s trade deficit with the EU as a percentage of its exports to the bloc increased from 13.5% in 2021 to 23.5% in 2025. At the same time, the country has not been able to significantly improve its trade surplus with other countries, indicating that Brexit perhaps did not help the U.K. in any considerable measure on the trade front.

Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and the resulting spike in energy prices benefited the U.K., which re-exported gas to EU countries. The Office for National Statistics reported that European demand, combined with Britain’s regasification infrastructure, which converted imported LNG back into pipeline gas, nearly tripled gas exports to record levels in April 2022 — possibly explaining the peak of £202.9 billion worth of goods exported to EU countries in 2022. However, U.K.’s goods exports haven’t recovered to their 2019 pre-pandemic peak. Inflation-adjusted goods exports remained weaker in 2025 than before the pandemic and before the U.K.-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement took effect in 2021.

On services, the U.K.’s exports to EU and non-EU countries follow largely parallel trends. Though services exports fell sharply during the pandemic, they have recovered since, suggesting that Brexit did not derail them — although sectors dependent on moving staff, particularly in EU countries, faced higher regulatory costs.

Source: Office for National Statistics, Government of the U.K.

(Gauri Singavarapu is interning with The Hindu’s Data Team)

World.title: Registration mandatory for drones weighing above 250 grams
World.content:
District Collector Vinay Goyal has issued fresh guidelines regulating the registration, possession, and transfer of drones and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) in Malappuram. The guidelines are in line with directions from the Union Ministry of Civil Aviation and the State government.

Under the order, all drones weighing more than 250 grams must be registered through the Digital Sky portal and obtain a unique identification number (UIN). The portal must also be updated with details of the new owner whenever a drone is sold or transferred.

The order prohibits the operation of drones in restricted areas without prior permission and the possession or use of unregistered drones. Violations will attract penal action, warned an official statement here.

Mr. Goyal has directed the police, tahsildars, and heads of district-level departments to ensure strict enforcement of the guidelines as part of security measures.

World.title: Can’t PM be trusted on appointing CEC, government asks Supreme Court
World.content:
The Union government questioned in the Supreme Court on Thursday (July 30, 2026) the insistence on having the Chief Justice of India (CJI) on the Prime Minister’s panel which selects the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), saying if the decision of the Prime Minister cannot be trusted then an “outsider” or a former judge must sit in to advice on the appointment of Cabinet Ministers too.

The Centre’s submission came while hearing petitions challenging the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service, and Term of Office) Act of 2023.

The petitions have contended that the Act “defeated” a Constitution Bench judgment in the Anoop Baranwal case, which had constituted a CEC selection panel chaired by the Prime Minister and including the Opposition Leader in the Lok Sabha and the CJI. The 2023 Act, passed within months of the judgment, had replaced the Chief Justice with a Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

Also Read | CJI to shift challenge to 2023 CEC appointment law to another Bench

A Bench headed by Justice Dipankar Datta had, in past hearings, questioned the lack of even “one absolutely neutral person” on the Prime Minister’s committee. The court had remarked that a Cabinet Minister would hardly defy the Prime Minister. The court had said the “dominant” presence of the Executive in the selection panel would send wrong signals to the public.

“If the Prime Minister’s decision is not to be trusted, why not have someone from outside or a former judge to select the Ministers also,” Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the government, asked on Thursday.

Mr. Mehta, quoting from a 2014 apex court judgment in the Manoj Narula case, said the Prime Minister’s office held constitutional trust and high sanctity. The law officer asked if a constitutional court, while deciding the composition of a committee in a statute, could presume abuse of power, bad faith and mala fide intention on part of the constitutional functionaries.

Justice Datta said the question was not about “lack of faith” in the Prime Minister, but about the principle of “justice not only being done, but shown to be done”.

Also Read | CJI was only meant to have a say in CEC/EC appointments till Parliament brought a law: Supreme Court

“The appointment procedure should be shown to be fair… The issue is that the composition of this committee tilts in favour of one side. There is a two versus one here, two of the Executive and one of the Opposition. Should there not be a show of fairness in the appointment to one of the most important offices of this country,” Justice Datta asked the Union government.

Mr. Mehta queried whether the Anoop Baranwal judgment could really restrict the wisdom of the Parliament to replace the CJI with a Cabinet Minister on the CEC selection panel. Like independence of the judiciary, the Constitution has also envisaged independence for the Legislative and Executive, the Solicitor General said.

At this juncture in the hearing, Justice Datta referred to the government’s oft-repeated complaint about the Collegium system of “judges selecting judges”.

“We wonder whether judges are really selecting judges nowadays,” Justice Datta said in a veiled comment about Executive interference in judicial appointments to the highest courts.

Also Read | Supreme Court asks if there was a ‘proper debate’ in Parliament before enacting CEC/EC appointments law

The court reserved judgment on the point whether the case should be referred to a five-judge Constitution Bench. Advocate Kaleeswaram Raj, on the petitioners’ side, said a reference was uncalled for as no novel question relating to constitutional interpretation has been identified or framed, other than the ones already dealt with in the Anoop Baranwal judgment.

The judgment by a Constitution Bench in March 2023 had declared that the CEC should be a person of “fierce independence, neutrality and honesty”. It had called for an end to government monopoly and “exclusive control” over appointments to the highest poll body.

Prior to the judgment, the CEC and ECs were appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. The judgment had brought the appointment process on par with that of the CBI Director.

World.title: Fresh probe ordered into Chembur tree collapse a month after boy’s death
World.content:
A month after 11-year-old Vihaan Srivastava was killed when a large peepal tree crashed onto his school bus in Mumbai’s Chembur, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has appointed an independent one-member committee, headed by noted botanist and former Mumbai University Vice-Chancellor Dr Sanjay V. Deshmukh, to conduct a fresh inquiry into the incident. The committee has been asked to submit its report within a month.

The move comes two weeks after Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde rejected the preliminary inquiry conducted by a civic panel appointed by Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide. The Mayor said the report failed to adequately examine the gravity of the incident and lacked recommendations on accountability and stringent action.

On Wednesday, The Indian Express reported that despite the Mayor’s July 16 directive seeking a second inquiry, the civic administration had yet to appoint a new panel.

The earlier inquiry had concluded that neither the BMC’s Roads Department nor its Garden and Tree Department was responsible for the incident. It said the Garden and Tree Department had pruned the tree and issued two notices — in April 2025 and January 2026 — to the Roads Department, advising precautionary measures while stormwater drainage work was carried out near the tree.

The report also stated that the Roads Department had taken steps to protect the tree by constructing the stormwater drain away from its roots.

A day after the incident, the BMC suspended three officials — an assistant superintendent from the Garden and Tree Department, a sub-engineer and an assistant engineer from the Roads Department.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the BMC said the newly appointed committee will review the methodology adopted by the earlier inquiry panel, reassess the evidence collected, scientifically evaluate its findings, identify the root cause of the tree collapse, and examine whether the interim measures and recommendations made in the initial report were adequate.



The committee will also assess the incident from multiple disciplinary perspectives, including botany, environmental science, engineering, road construction, drainage, soil science, climate and public administration. It has also been tasked with recommending policy reforms to strengthen Mumbai’s tree management system and prevent similar incidents in the future.

Speaking to The Indian Express, BJP corporator and Leader of the House Ganesh Khankar said, “It’s a rational decision to appoint an independent committee. Had the probe been carried out by the BMC’s own committee, we would not have accepted the report.”

World.title: Manjalpur Assembly bypoll: Congress protests ‘BJP rally’ on polling day, ruling party calls it ‘voter awareness using drums’
World.content:
The Manjalpur Assembly bypoll witnessed a political flashpoint within hours of polling on Thursday as Congress leaders staged a protest outside the Vadodara Collector’s chamber accusing the Election Commission of turning a blind eye to what they called BJP campaigning on the voting day.

The protest began after Vadodara City Congress president Rutvij Joshi accused BJP leaders and elected representatives of openly campaigning on the polling day by moving through Manjalpur wearing party scarves and accompanied by drums, in violation of election rules. Joshi said videos of the alleged violations had been sent to the district administration but no action had been taken.



Congress leaders met the District Collector seeking action and alleged that their representation was not heard, prompting them to stage a sit-in protest outside the Collector’s chamber, raising slogans accusing the Election Commission of acting in favour of the BJP. “The Election Commission is showing partiality. BJP leaders are openly campaigning on the counting day and despite our complaints, there has been no police action.. The EC must stop acting as an instrument of the BJP,” Joshi said.

Congress leader Sandeep Mangrola, who submitted a written complaint to the Election officers, alleged that party workers who approached the police to lodge complaints were made to wait at the police station while BJP leaders continued campaigning in different parts of the constituency.

Justifying the action, the ruling BJP claimed that the party was not campaigning but “creating awareness on the need to vote”. BJP general secretary Hitendrasinh Chauhan said: Our party workers had gone to create voter awareness and encourage people to exercise their right to vote freely. Voting is the democratic right of every citizen… They used drums while urging the people to vote.”



“Some anti-social elements associated with the Congress, (allegedly) under the influence of alcohol, attacked and intimidated our workers. Despite the provocation, our workers showed great restraint. They were assaulted, and the mobile phones of several workers were snatched away… After the police arrived at the scene, the situation was brought under control. Our workers are now safe, and we have informed the police about the entire incident,” he said.

In a statement on Thursday, the District Election officers said that to ensure that the polling process during the Manjalpur Assembly by-election was conducted in a completely transparent, free, fair, and peaceful manner, webcasting facilities were arranged at all 260 polling stations.

“For effective monitoring of the polling process, two cameras were installed at each polling station. A total of 520 cameras enabled continuous live monitoring of all polling stations. To effectively monitor the live webcast feeds, a zonal webcasting viewing team was deployed at the Assembly Hall. The team comprised 28 personnel, with one official assigned to each zone… Throughout the polling period, all polling stations were under constant observation through the webcasting system. The monitoring was aimed at detecting any untoward incident, irregularity, or violation of the Model Code of Conduct,” the statement said.

Clash



A separate clash occurred outside Panchsheel Vidyalaya polling station in Manjalpur between two groups, including the Congress workers. The party alleged that one of its workers was assaulted during the altercation.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Abhishek Gupta said police rushed to the spot after receiving information about the clash and dispersed the crowd. He said polling resumed peacefully and added that CCTV footage from the area would be examined as part of the investigation. District Election offices were unavailable for comments on the Congress’ representation.

38% turnout till 6 pm

Voting began at 7 am across 260 polling stations at 62 locations, with about 38 per cent turnout recorded between 7 am and 6 pm. More than 2.19 lakh voters, including around 1.11 lakh men and 1.07 lakh women, are eligible to vote in the bypoll, which has emerged as a direct contest between BJP’s Satish Patel and Congress’ Bhikhabhai Rabari. The by-election was necessitated by the death of BJP MLA Yogesh Patel in June.



The bypoll is being closely watched as Manjalpur has long been considered a BJP stronghold. In the 2022 Assembly election, Yogesh Patel won the seat by a margin of over one lakh votes, securing 1,20,133 votes against the Congress candidate’s around 19,000. The BJP is seeking to retain its dominance in the constituency, while the Congress is hoping to narrow the gap in one of Vadodara city’s most politically significant seats.

Who is VK Kamakoti

World.title: Indian Railways to allow online booking of personal luggage on confirmed train tickets from July 31
World.content:
Indian Railways Online Personal Luggage Booking: Indian Railways is set to introduce online booking of personal luggage for passengers holding confirmed train tickets from July 31. The new facility is aimed at making luggage booking more convenient and streamlining the parcel booking process.

In a letter dated July 20, 2026, the Railway Board directed all zonal railways to implement online booking of personal luggage up to the prescribed weight limit for passengers travelling on confirmed tickets.
